ASSAULT HORROR Girl, 16, sexually assaulted after being followed on train by man as cops share CCTV of person they want to speak to

COPS have released CCTV images of a man after a teenage girl was allegedly sexually assaulted on a train.

The victim, 16, reported she was sexually assaulted on an Elizabeth Line train in London on Wednesday July 8.

At around 12.40pm she boarded a bus towards Abbey Wood Underground station.

A man followed her onto the bus and watched her throughout the journey.





The girl noticed him looking and he followed her off the bus where she disembarked.

She got onto a train at Abbey Wood towards Tottenham Court Road, with the man trailing behind her.

When she arrived at Tottenham Court Road station, the girl left the train and the man pursued her.

He allegedly then approached and sexually assaulted her before fleeing the scene.

Detectives would like to speak to the man pictured, as they believe he holds vital information.

Anyone who recognises him is asked to contact British Transport Police by texting 61016 or by calling 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 119 of 9 July.

Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: X-rated texts sent between married prison guard, 27, & ‘jail lag she had sex with’ revealed as details of tryst emerge
News.content:
'BIG MAN HANDS' X-rated texts sent between married prison guard, 27, & ‘jail lag she had sex with’ revealed as details of tryst emerge

A TROVE of dirty messages to an inmate have been uncovered as a married prison guard faces charges of sexual abuse.

Correctional officer Jordan Pensak, 27, is accused of having sex with a prisoner on multiple occasions – sending him messages detailing her desire for his “big man hands”, according to court documents.



Over 100 sexually explicit messages, photos and videos, were discovered on Pensak’s phone, court documents reveal.

Last week she was charged with one count of sexual abuse of an individual in federal custody.



Court documents say that on multiple occasions Pensak had sex with the unidentified inmate in her office at the Federal Correctional Institution in Fort Dix, New Jersey.

Prosecutors allege the inmate would pay other prisoners to act as “lookouts” during their hook-ups.

Text messages found on Pensak’s phone reveal her lust for the felon’s “big man hands”, prosecutors alege.

The inmate offered to buy Pensak “vibrating panties”, in one alleged sordid exchange in 2025 according to court documents.

In February, she allegedly texted a freind: “We freak nast [I] keep telling you this.”

“Only thing he wont do is let me in them cheeks.”



Investigators say she raised concerns about believing the inmate had impregnated her.

The complaint and statements made in court said: “In one of those communications Pensak raised concerns that she might be pregnant with the inmate’s child.”

According to the complaint, Penask – in a text exchange with a former inmate – said: “I’m 3 days late for my period you ready to be an uncle?”

“That aint good for the investigation.”

She later allegedly said: “I know I couldn’t keep it. And to go through all that without him would be hard on me.”



In another text message with a friend, Pensak was asked if the relationship involved sex or contraband, to which she allegedly replied, “both”, according to court documents.

When she was asked if she knew she could be criminally charged, she responded “Yes I know,” according to the the court documents.

In texts she allegedly said she believed one of the other inmates “snitched” on them, but insisted “they can’t prove nothing.”

Pensak was charged with sexual abuse and was released on bail, according to the US Attorney’s Office.

The complaint and statements made in court continued: “Pensak had a consensual sexual relationship with an inmate at Fort Dix and had sex with him in January 2026.



“Pensak and the inmate also exchanged sexually explicit photographs and messages over social media and electronic applications, facilitated by the inmate’s use of two contraband cell phones while in custody at Fort Dix.

“Pensak admitted to having a sexual relationship with the inmate in text messages sent to multiple individuals, including family members of the inmate.”

She faces a maximum of 15 years behind bars if convicted.

A spokesperson for the Federal Bureau of Prisons confirmed to The Post that Pensak has been placed on administrative leave pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

News.title: Cabinet minister forced to defend Andy Burnham’s decision to take holiday just 15 days into premiership
News.content:
A CABINET Minister was forced to defend Andy Burnham for taking a holiday just 15 days into his Premiership.

The new PM was warned by a senior Labour backbencher that he was making a “mistake”.



Backbencher Graham Stringer told Talk: “He will come to regret it.”

But Justice Secretary Alex Norris insisted the PM – whose location is being kept secret by No10 – will be “in constant contact with his office”.



He added: “ I mean, I might gently say that I’ve spoken to him virtually every day since I joined the cabinet, and I suspect that won’t change.”

Downing Street said Andy Burnham would be taking some time off to spend it with his wife and family. Number 10 refused to say where he was travelling.

Louise Haigh – previously sacked by ex-PM Sir Keir Starmer over a fraud conviction – is in charge as Mr Burnham’s deputy while he is away from his desk.

It is common for Prime Ministers to take a break in August when Parliament is not sitting.

But Mr Burnham is by far the earliest UK premier to take a holiday after just 15 days into the job he has craved all of his life.

Parliament will return in early September for a couple of weeks before a second recess for the party conference season.



Theresa May comes second closest after jetting off after just four weeks.

Within recent years Rishi Sunak took the longest to take time off after working non-stop for nine months after becoming Prime Minister.

Reform UK blasted Mr Burnham for taking a break this early in his premiership.



Chairman Lee Anderson MP said: “Two weeks into the job and Andy Burnham has already had enough.

“After dropping a number of unfunded commitments and overseeing over 2,000 illegal migrants breaking into our country he’s bunked off for a jolly abroad. This isn’t a Prime Minister that’s serious about leading.”

The Prime Minister also told Elizabeth Day on the How To Fail podcast his wife was shocked he wanted to run again as Labour leader.

He said: “’What? Not again. They told you twice they don’t want you. Why are you doing it again?’”

“No, we’ve always just had honest conversations about it.”



Mr Burnham added: “She took some persuading, to be honest, because I guess she didn’t want to see me go through it all again and then end out on the wrong side, at the end of it. But she gives me good advice.”

Downing Street refused to say where the PM would be travelling.

He will be accompanied by security.

News.title: Mystical UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ is put up for sale – and it’s even featured in a blockbuster TV show
News.content:
HELL OF A BUY Mystical UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ is put up for sale – and it’s even featured in a blockbuster TV show

A MYSTICAL UK beauty spot dubbed the ‘Devil’s Pulpit’ has been put up for sale – but the price remains a mystery.

The breathtaking Finnich Glen in Stirlingshire, Scotland, has been featured in blockbuster TV shows, including Outlander.



Tucked away 15 miles outside Glasgow near Killearn and Drymen, the beautiful 23-acre sandstone gorge attracts 70,000 visitors every year.

Adventurers flock to the site to tackle the 1.5-mile trail, clambering down ancient steps to swim in the gorge.



Formed between 10,000 and 12,000 years ago by melting glaciers, the 80ft-deep gorge is steeped in dark folklore.

Local tales link it to ancient druids, witches, and the Devil himself.

TV fans will recognise its roaring waterfall as “St Ninian’s Spring” from the smash-hit drama Outlander.

The sandstone bedrock, which appears to run blood red due to the sediment in the water, means the gorge has been a popular set for television and film.



Hits such as Sherlock Holmes, Taggart, Pokemon Detective Pikachu and King Arthur have all used the stunning location.

After previously being put on the market in 2023, the spectacular Devil’s Pulpit has gone up for sale again, but without a clear asking price.

However, potential buyers will be pleased to learn that there is approved planning permission for a brand-new visitor centre.



It will be complete with a cafe, restaurant, event space, and dedicated car park.

The upgrades are expected to increase visitor numbers to more than 300,000 a year.

Commercial estate agents Christie & Co are handling the sale on an “offers invited” basis.

The current owners said: “We feel that we have reached a stage in life where new owners would be able to take forward our vision for the Glen and develop this opportunity in a way that is compatible with this unique property.

“The Glen requires management to preserve and protect its environment, but whoever purchases Finnich Glen, taking it to the next phase, has the opportunity to follow in the footsteps of giants.”



Mark Lavery, director of retail and leisure at Christie & Co, said: “This opportunity will appeal to buyers who want to create a commercial business and unique visitor experience with national importance, against a stunning backdrop.

“Historically important, and already a tourist attraction with approved planning permission, the development opportunities are exciting, and we encourage interested parties to get in touch.”

News.title: Dad, 66, desperately tried to save daughter, 32, after she was dragged into sea at surfing beach before both drowned
News.content:
DOUBLE TRAGEDY Dad, 66, desperately tried to save daughter, 32, after she was dragged into sea at surfing beach before both drowned

A DAD and a daughter drowned after he desperately tried to save her as she was dragged out to sea at a popular surfing beach, an inquest heard.

John Collins, 66, and Samantha Collins, 32, both died on Fistral Beach in Newquay, Cornwall on Sunday July 26.



The inquest at Cornwall Coroner’s Court in Truro heard on Tuesday that John, a retired technical manager from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, had been on holiday in Newquay with his daughter Samantha and wife Adele Collins.

The pair were pulled out of the water unconscious by surfers and beachgoers and sadly were pronounced dead at the scene.



Assistant Coroner for Cornwall & Isles of Scilly, Emma Hillson, told the court: “John and Samantha were fishing on rocks when Samantha was dragged into the sea.

“John tried to save her but very sadly was unable to do so and both lost their lives.”



In both cases Ms Hillson gave a provisional cause of death as drowning and adjourned the inquest until 19 July 2027.

The 750-metre-long Fistral Beach has massive winter wave swells and is known as the “home of British surfing”, drawing up to one million visitors each year.



Witness Jamie Stockwell previously revealed how he plunged into the sea fully dressed in a bid to save Samantha.

He said: “I jumped in with all my clothes on. I didn’t realise how deep it was. It was very powerful swell, and I was lucky I wasn’t another casualty.

“We were being hurled on to the rocks. I managed to push her up and her boyfriend pulled her up by the arms and started to try to give her mouth-to-mouth.

“We tried to give her CPR for about ten minutes. I was trying to keep her partner calm as he was in pieces.”

Sand Phoenix, who was on the Beach when the tragedy unfolded, revealed he “sprinted” up to help after seeing John go in after his daughter.



The 33-year-old added: “He had been pulled out of the water but had been in there about seven minutes.

“I had an adrenaline pen which I jabbed him with and tried to give him oxygen but his lungs were full of water and there was no response.

“The paramedics arrived and carried on trying to give CPR. He was still wearing his trousers so I don’t think he had been swimming.

“It looks like they had been walking near the rocks and had fallen in.”

One eyewitness who was staying in a van overlooking the beach said: “First thing I heard was a man shouting ‘we need ropes, they are drowning’.



“I made my way down there and there were two people in the water, a lady next to me spotted a body floating in the water and the other one was already on the beach with people.

“A woman on the cliff was desperately trying to ring her husband and daughter but neither was picking up.”

Cops earlier said Samantha entered the water carrying a peach or orange coloured handbag which has not been recovered.

The leather-style bag is said to contain a number of personal items of “great sentimental value to her loved ones” as the force appeal for it to be handed in if found.

Cops said in a statement: “Police were called by the South Western Ambulance Service at around 9.45pm on Sunday 26 July following reports that two people had been recovered from the water at Fistral Beach, Newquay.



“Emergency services attended and a cordon was put in place, which has since been removed.

“Sadly, a woman in her 30s and a man in his 60s were pronounced deceased at the scene.

“Their families have been informed, and our thoughts are with them at this extremely difficult time.”

News.title: BP boss warns Andy Burnham to ramp up North Sea drilling and U-turn on damaging tax hikes on sector
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has been told to ramp up North Sea oil and gas drilling and think twice about damaging tax hikes on the sector, BP’s boss warns.

The Prime Minister is facing pressure to further exploit the domestic energy supplies after the industry hit out at their windfall tax.



The intervention comes as BP announced quarterly profits of £4.26billion – its highest since the start of the Ukraine war in 2022 – as prices rise due to the Middle East conflict.

The energy giant’s chief Meg O’Neill remarks came after the firm last week announced they are are selling their UK operations after six decades there.



She said: “We do still see growth potential in the North Sea – there’s still undeveloped fields there. We would love to see exploration resume in the North Sea.”

Labour hiked the windfall tax, the Energy Profits Levy, to 38 per cent, bringing the total headine tax rate on the North Sea oil and gas firms to 78 per cent.



O’Neill said that from an investment viewpoint “dollars spent in the North Sea are just not as competitive as other opportunities.”

It comes as Donald Trump said the UK was “sitting on top of gold”.

Speaking from the White House on Monday evening, the US President added: “When you look at the UK, they have one of the best energy fields in the world, North Sea oil.

“Now I think your new Prime Minister is going to actually open up the (North Sea), from what I hear.



“I spoke to him, and he sounded terrific on this subject. But you open it up, you’ll be a wealthy country.

“You keep it closed, you’re going to be a bankrupt country, which is what you are now. Essentially, you’re a bankrupt country.”

He added: “You’re sitting on top of gold, better than gold, and you don’t do anything with it.”

News.title: Moment high speed train smashes through hay bales and tractor’s trailer after drunk farmer stops on level crossing
News.content:
THIS is the moment a train smashes through a hay-filled trailer after an intoxicated farmer stops on a level crossing.

Crazy footage shows bales hay thrown into the air as the train collides with the trailer at high speed.



The incident occurred around midday on August 3 at a railway crossing in Tczew County, in the north of Poland.

It is understood 500 people were on the train at the time of the crash.



One passenger said: “I was sitting in the first carriage, and the impact was felt strongly.”

The footage, released by Polish State Railways, shows the tractor hauling trailers loaded with straw bales crossing the railway as barriers closed and warning lights flashed.

The driver then comes to a stop with the trailers still on the tracks before a passenger train crashes through them.

The organisation said the tractor driver was found to be intoxicated.



Officials confirmed that the tractor driver ignored signals and entered the crossing just as a train was approaching.

The approaching train failed to stop in time.

Thankfully there were no reported injuries.



Local media report the driver, a 67- year-old man, is likely to face criminal charges.

Railway workers remind passengers that at every level crossing, the train always has the right of way.

Polish State Railways Linie Kolejowe said: “A rail-road crossing is no place for recklessness. Stop, look around. Strictly follow the regulations, pay attention to signs and signals.”

According to the Office of Rail Transport, nearly 200 accidents and collisions occur at level crossings in Poland each year.

Last year 185 accidents and collisions were recorded resulting in 58 deaths and 18 serious injuries.



It comes as two trains were involved in a head on collision in late July in Poland.

Three people were injured after the carriages derailed on impact.

News.title: Millions of police hours will be saved by scrapping woke liaison officers, Tory plans claim
News.content:
MILLIONS of police hours will be saved by scrapping woke liaison officers, Tory plans say.

They include using AI and scaling back equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) roles to free up 3,800 bobbies on the beat.



Kemi Badenoch’s party will remove all woke jobs from the police force and reallocate those workers to the front line, which alone will save 500,000 hours of police time per year.

Taxpayers are continuing to foot the bill for hundreds of EDI officers across the service.



Race action plans to smooth relations with ethnic minority communities will also be slashed and stripped of cash.

And cops who want to form identity groups on their race or gender are free to do so in their own time, but must foot the bill themselves.



Mrs Badenoch said her “common sense” proposals meant more police officers could be on the streets fighting crime.

She said: “We have spoken to officers and developed a plan that will mean less time spent on paperwork and more spent on keeping people safe.”

The Tories are keen on cutting out the need for cops to fill out the lengthy forms demanded by Government lawyers after every single case.

Officers spend 23 minutes doing paperwork every time they get handcuffs out.



Scrapping this will cut 425,000 forms and save 163,000 hours of police time a year.

New plans would only make police officers fill out paperwork when force is used.

Tory Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “The more time officers spend filling out forms and box ticking is time they are not on the streets or solving crimes.”

News.title: Hornsea missing boy live: Huge rescue operation as teen vanishes off Yorkshire coast
News.content:
HM Coastguard is involved in the massive search operation off the East Yorkshire coast

Emergency services are searching for a 13-year-old boy who went missing while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast

A huge search is underway after a 13-year-old boy went missing while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 6pm following reports that a boy had got into difficulty in the water.

Emergency crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, are involved in the search. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat has also been launched.

Chief Superintendent Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: SpaceX rocket on collision course with Moon - how you could watch it from Earth
News.content:
SpaceX rocket on collision course with Moon - how you could watch it from Earth

A drifting SpaceX rocket will slam into the Moon on Wednesday, with scientists saying the 'impact flash' could be visible from Earth

View 2 Images A section of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will slam into the Moon on Wednesday (Image: Geoffrey Swaine/REX/Shutterstock)

A drifting SpaceX rocket is on a collision course with the Moon - and the impact flash could be visible from Earth.

‌



The rocket’s upper stage, about the size of a five-storey building, will unintentionally slam into the Moon on Wednesday, carving out a crater and sending up a plume of dust and rubble.

‌



The Falcon 9 rocket was launched by SpaceX last year as part of a US-Japanese mission carrying two lunar landers and scientific equipment to the Moon.

‌



The abandoned segment measures around 40ft and weighs around 10,000lb. Experts say the crash could have been avoided if the upper stage had been nudged into orbit around the Sun.

View 2 Images A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying the company's Dragon spacecraft is launched on NASA's SpaceX Crew-9 mission to the International Space Station in September 2024 (Image: NASA via Getty Images)

Space-tracking expert Bill Gray predicts the rocket will strike the Moon at around 5,400mph - about seven times the speed of sound. He believes the impact will be near Einstein Crater on the Moon's sunlit western limb.

‌



Will the collision be visible from Earth?

The collision itself is not expected to be visible from Earth. However, some astronomers believe the impact flash - which will last less than a second - may be visible through powerful telescopes.

The plume of dust and debris is considered more likely to be visible. It could stretch for several miles above the lunar surface and remain visible through telescopes for tens of minutes.

Astronomer Bill Gray, who first identified the rocket stage's eventual lunar collision, wrote on his Project Pluto website : "Maybe we'll see the flash. Maybe we'll see rocks ejected from the crater. Maybe we'll even see both."

‌



Dr Matt Bothwell, public astronomer at the University of Cambridge, told the BBC that people with access to a sophisticated telescope may be able to spot a flash radiating off the Moon's surface.

Observers in the eastern US and Canada, along with much of South America, are expected to have the best chance of seeing it.

Growing concern over space junk

While scientists are not too concerned about this particular piece of space junk, they say it highlights the growing threat as more and more items cram into orbit.

‌



"Things are getting crowded up there," said Gray, who plans to view the aftermath from New Brunswick, Canada.

It will be the second discarded rocket known to crash into the Moon accidentally. A Chinese rocket segment dug out a pair of craters on the Moon's far side in 2022.

Los Alamos National Laboratory’s Benjamin Fernando told The Associated Press: "Part of the reason for our interest in this event is to figure out how much of a hazard debris impacts pose to future astronauts."

Article continues below

Fernando expects the impact to create a crater about 90ft across and 16ft deep - too small to be seen from Earth but visible to spacecraft.

Retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell told The Associated Press that "this impact will not be a problem", but said that "in a future where there are long-term bases on the Moon, similar impacts would be an issue, and we need not to leave rocket stages in chaotic orbits of this kind".

News.title: Ed Miliband to tell Donald Trump's White House ending Iran war will bring down prices
News.content:
Ed Miliband to tell Donald Trump's White House ending Iran war will bring down prices

The senior Cabinet minister is set to discuss Russia’s illegal war in Ukraine and the Middle East conflict as he meets with senior members of the Trump administration

View 2 Images Ed Miliband will hold talks with US officials on Wednesday (Image: Getty Images)

Ed Miliband is set to urge Donald Trump's White House to secure a lasting ceasefire in Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease the cost of living for Brits.

‌



The senior Cabinet minister is set to discuss Russia ’s illegal war in Ukraine and the Middle East conflict as he meets with senior members of the Trump administration for the first time since taking up the role.

‌



Mr Miliband will meet with the US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday, who invited the Foreign Secretary to Washington DC after their first meeting at ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) in Manila.

‌



It comes after the erratic US President said he believed he and the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham are “going to have a very good relationship” as he again stressed the need for the UK to tackle immigration and open up North Sea oil - before claiming Britain was currently “a bankrupt country".

View 2 Images US Secretary of State Marco Rubio invited Ed Miliband to Washington (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The Foreign Secretary and Secretary of State are expected to discuss a range of issues, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz, to help ease the cost-of-living crisis.

Mr Miliband said: “I am greatly looking forward to my second meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in which we will discuss the ongoing work to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and secure a lasting ceasefire, which is essential to ease cost of living pressures on British families.

“We will also discuss how we can continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine against Russia's war- as well as the importance of addressing the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza and working towards a lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis.”

Article continues below

Mr Miliband has previously branded Trump a “racist, misogynistic self-confessed groper”, who had “lowered the bar for idiocy.”

In the meetings, Mr Miliband is expected to stress that Ukraine's security is inseparable from the rest of Europe, and reiterate the UK's commitment to stand with Kyiv for as long as it takes.

He will also discuss the importance of addressing the urgent humanitarian situation in Gaza and redoubling international efforts to secure a lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis.

News.title: UK weather maps show Brits to bake in new heatwave as 14 counties set for 35C+ temperatures - see full list
News.content:
UK weather maps show Brits to bake in new heatwave as 14 counties set for 35C+ temperatures - see full list

The latest WXCharts maps show temperatures will gradually climb across southern and eastern England, with many areas forecast to reach at least 30C in the coming days

View 3 Images Weather maps are red - because it is getting hotter (Image: WXCHARTS)

These striking weather maps show the UK is soon set to swelter in temperatures of up to 36C.

‌



Forecasters say temperatures will slowly climb and, by Wednesday August 12, much of the country will be sweltering in the heat again. The warmest counties will be those in the south and east of England, including Cambridgeshire and Norfolk.

‌



The latest WXCharts maps are, in most, a bright red, which indicates temperatures will be hot. Meteorologists at Metdesk, which issued the maps, say the mercury could peak at 36C on or around Wednesday August 12.

‌



But, during this period, temperatures are widely expected to exceed 30C, including across parts of the Midlands and northern England. Scotland and Northern Ireland are expected to remain noticeably cooler, with many areas forecast to stay in the low to mid-20s.

While it will be warmest in the east, it will still be dry and sunny across Wales — albeit cooler here too. Forecasters believe it will be 26C or 27C in and around Swansea, for instance.

View 3 Images People have fun at a beach in Folkestone, Kent (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



As the Express reports, it was warm on Monday with a 33.5C high recorded by the Met Office in Wisley, Surrey. However, rain is expected on Wednesday and Thuirsday, heaviest across Northern Ireland and parts of Scotland.

A yellow weather warning is in place for thunderstorms across Angus, Perth and Kinross, Aberdeen, Aberdeenshire, Moray and Highland. The Met Office says: " Slow-moving heavy showers and thunderstorms may cause some disruption."

List of counties set for 35C+ highs next week

Bedfordshire

Berkshire

Buckinghamshire

Cambridgeshire

Essex

Leicestershire

‌



View 3 Images Edgbaston Reservoir in Birmingham is near depleted following the hot weather (Image: Getty Images)

The heatwaves have, though, led to warnings that shoppers face higher food prices and possible shortages because of the prolonged drought.

Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers’ Union, called on ministers to help support the building of reservoirs on farms as part of wider measures. He said: “Water security is food security and food security is part of our national security."

Article continues below

Parched conditions have caused havoc for farmers. Many arable farmers have been forced to bring forward their wheat harvest by several weeks - in some cases the earliest for at least 20 years - because of the extreme weather, with an impact on yields - the amount produced.

News.title: UK housebuilder falls into administration as customers hear homes left unfinished
News.content:
UK housebuilder falls into administration as customers hear homes left unfinished

Hood Property Cardrona Limited, based in Scotland, has plunged into administration and may now have to sell its land near Peebles in the Scottish Borders

View 2 Images A Scottish housebuilding company has entered administration (Image: Getty Images)

A UK housebuilder has fallen into administration, reportedly leaving homes unfinished and debts of over £4 million.

‌



Scottish company Hood Property Cardrona Limited has gone under and may now be forced to sell its land near the town of Peebles in the Scottish Borders, according to The Herald.

‌



Administrators said they had to "forcibly gain entry" to the closed site for 20 homes, where offers had already been accepted on "several" properties.

‌



However, more funding would have been needed "to finish building the properties and complete the development", administrators said in an update.

James Stephen and Kerry Bailey of BDO have been appointed joint administrators and have extended the administration period until September, reports the Express.

‌

News.title: 'Nigel Farage created the £250,000 by-election chaos — so he should answer for every penny spent'
News.content:
'Nigel Farage created the £250,000 by-election chaos — so he should answer for every penny spent'

Nigel Farage decided to quit as MP for Clacton-on-Sea, Essex, last month and now stands in a by-election there on Thursday, a stunt said to cost the taxpayer £250,000

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Nigel Farage has dumped the country with a £250,000 by-election bill for a stunt that reeks of vanity, evasion and contempt for taxpayers. He quit his seat only to stand again after rivals accused him of dodging scrutiny over a £5million gift from a Thai-based crypto billionaire.

‌



The result is a democratic farce: a near metre-long ballot paper, a record 34 candidates, Count Binface among them, and Tendring Council forced to spend scarce money on extraordinary arrangements. Farage never stops preaching about waste, bloated government and respect for the public purse.

‌



Yet when his own career is on the line, he is happy to burn through taxpayers’ cash without blinking. Clacton deserves a serious MP, not another circus built around one man’s ego.

‌



His party’s supposed crusade against waste looks utterly fraudulent. Farage called this election. He created the chaos. He should answer for every penny spent and explain why local people must pay for his latest exercise in self-preservation.

Hit banks with windfall tax

Together, HSBC, Lloyds, Barclays and NatWest raked in more than £29 billion in six months while families are hammered by mortgage costs, energy bills and high prices.

‌



Their profits have been swollen by interest rates staying higher for longer. The banks did not cause the crisis, but benefited handsomely from it. Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey should use the autumn Budget to impose a windfall tax on excess profits.

This levy would take a share of earnings made in exceptional circumstances while leaving banks with billions. The money could cut energy bills and support the NHS, schools, social care and councils. Taxpayers rescued the banks when they were in trouble. Now, families need help, ministers must make them return the favour.

Keep your cool with your fridge

Amid the heatwaves, Britain has lost the plot over the fridge. Apples, nuts and potatoes should apparently chill out, while chocolate, tomatoes and coffee belong outside.

Article continues below

Every kitchen has now become a rather chilly game of chance. That is the cold, hard truth.

News.title: Tuscany rocked by 'strong' earthquake as people flee buildings in Pisa and Lucca
News.content:
Tuscany rocked by 'strong' earthquake as people flee buildings in Pisa and Lucca

A 'strong' 4.3-magnitude earthquake struck near Pisa on Monday morning, with its epicentre just four miles from Italy's historic Tuscan city

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A "strong" 4.3-magnitude earthquake has rocked the Italian region of Tuscany - with its epicentre just four miles from the historic city of Pisa.

‌



The quake was felt at around 10.15am local time across northern Tuscany, including the provinces of Lucca, Pisa and Massa-Carrara.

‌



The epicentre was near San Piero a Grado, around seven kilometres from Pisa, at a shallow depth of around eight kilometres, according to Italy’s National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV).

‌



The relatively shallow depth contributed to the tremor being felt widely across northern Tuscany.

Tuscany regional governor Eugenio Giani wrote on social media: "Checks are currently under way with the regional emergency system. The strong earthquake was felt throughout northern Tuscany."

View 2 Images The Leaning Tower of Pisa and the Pisa Cathedral remained open to visitors (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A second tremor followed at 1.04pm, with the Italian National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) recording a 3.2-magnitude earthquake. The epicentre was around five kilometres from Pisa, at a depth of 11 kilometres.

Bernard Dika, undersecretary to the presidency of the Tuscany region, wrote on social media after the first quake: "Hundreds of calls have been made to the regional emergency number 112 following the strong earthquake recorded in Pisa, with many people taking to the streets.

"At the moment, there are no reports of injuries. Some precautionary evacuations are under way in the area."

‌



Three families were evacuated from a building in San Giuliano Terme, near Pisa, according to local newspaper Corriere Fiorentino. The earthquake caused structural instability at the property, requiring further inspections by firefighters. The evacuation was carried out as a precaution.

No injuries or other significant damage to buildings have been reported. In Pisa, firefighters received numerous calls following the earthquake, which prompted residents to leave their homes and gather in the streets as a precaution, Italian media reported.

Court hearings at the local courthouse were suspended, and the city hall was also evacuated as a safety measure. After inspections were completed, residents and employees were allowed to return to the buildings.

Article continues below

Rail services on the Pisa-Empoli, Pisa-Livorno, Pisa-Lucca and Pisa-Viareggio lines were suspended for around four hours - until 3.30pm local time - to allow technical checks on the infrastructure, according to Corriere Fiorentino.

The Leaning Tower of Pisa and other museums and monuments in Piazza dei Miracoli were not affected by the earthquake and remain open to visitors.

News.title: Afghan boxer arrested in Greece over discovery of Scottish woman's body in suitcase
News.content:
The man suspected of killing Scottish aid worker Elisabeth Jane Ross in Greece is 26-year-old Sharif Ahmadzai, the BBC understands.

He was arrested after the body of the 38-year-old was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, several days after she was reported missing.

Ahmadzai, who was born in Afghanistan and is a champion boxer, settled in Greece after travelling there as a teenager.

Both Ross and Ahmadzai had worked with refugees and Greek police are investigating whether the pair knew each other through the charity sector.

Ahmadzai was arrested on suspicion of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences, and is expected to appear in court in Athens on Wednesday.

Police said the coroner's initial report failed to determine a cause of death, but more detailed examinations concluded it was an "obvious criminal act, likely asphyxiation".

News.title: Infantino calls executive meeting as criticism mounts
News.content:
Gianni Infantino has summoned senior leaders of football's world governing body to a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday, after another day in which its president has faced fierce criticism of his plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations.

Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, and Prince Ali, president of the Jordanian Football Association, all made clear their opposition to Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise.

Infantino, who has been in Morocco over the past week, called an executive meeting in Rabat as he attempts to find a solution to the controversy.

Wenger said in a statement issued through Fifa that scrapping the plan was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Grafstrom called the last week "a sad and reproachable series of events" in an internal email to Fifa staff.

Prince Ali, meanwhile, accused Fifa of creating a situation which "amounts to blackmail" over unpaid prize money and support for Infantino's re-election.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions, since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from the body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

News.title: Princess Eugenie gives birth to baby girl in Portugal
News.content:
Princess Eugenie has given birth to a baby girl at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

The baby was born on Monday at 18:20 BST, weighing 6lbs 9oz.

This is Princess Eugenie's third child with her husband, Jack Brooksbank, following the births of her sons August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, who was born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, who was born in 2023.

A statement from Buckingham Palace read: "Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

In a post on Instagram, the princess, 36, wrote: "Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

"We are beyond in love with our girlie."

They are yet to announce a name.

The new arrival - who will not be an HRH - will be 15th in line to the throne, moving ahead of their great-uncle the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Edward.

The couple live between Portugal and Ivy Cottage, in the grounds of Kensington Palace.

They announced Princess Eugenie's pregnancy in May. She posted a photograph of her young sons holding a baby scan with the caption: "Baby Brooksbank due 2026!"

The Palace said on social media at the time: "His Majesty The King has been informed and is delighted with the news."

News.title: Major search under way for boy, 13, missing at sea
News.content:
A major search is under way for a 13-year-old boy who reportedly got into difficulty while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast, police have said.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 18:00 BST.

Crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, remain at the scene. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat joined the search.

Ch Supt Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

News.title: Bono, Eddie Vedder and Hozier among mourners at Glen Hansard's funeral
News.content:
Stars from the world of music including U2's Bono, Pearl Jam's lead singer Eddie Vedder, and Hozier, attended the funeral of Glen Hansard on Tuesday.

The 56-year-old Oscar-winning Irish singer and songwriter died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin last week.

Hansard, who shot to prominence in 1991 musical comedy film The Commitments, was long-time frontman of acclaimed rock band The Frames.

News of his sudden death shocked the music world and fans alike, with tributes being paid from the likes of Ed Sheeran and Bruce Springsteen, who said he was "heartbroken".

News.title: Athletes go 'missing' after Commonwealth Games ends
News.content:
Several athletes have disappeared after competing in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, failing to return home with the rest of their teams.

Police Scotland said it had received reports of various athletes "unaccounted for" in the aftermath of the Games, which concluded on Sunday.

The sports website NBS Sport, external said four members of the Ugandan boxing squad had not turned up to fly home, adding that one member of the team had told the website the athletes intended to seek asylum in Scotland.

Pakistan Today also reported, external that the boxer Qudratullah had not joined the rest of his team mates in flying home to Pakistan, and that he was not found in his room when officials went to search for him.

News.title: Care company fined for running illegal children's homes in legal first
News.content:
A care company has been prosecuted and fined for running illegal children's homes in what has been called the first case of its kind.

Catalyst Care Limited is the first unregistered children's homes provider to be successfully prosecuted, according to Ofsted, which brought the legal action against it.

Its directors pleaded guilty at Croydon Magistrates' Court in relation to failing to register children's homes and have been fined a total of Â£92,400.

The Croydon company operated three homes in Kent between 2022-2025 which accommodated up to nine children. During this time the homes received over Â£1.7m million in payments from local authorities.

Ofsted said this was despite it repeatedly warning directors they were breaking the law.

All children's homes in England must register with Ofsted, and managing a home without a registration is a criminal offence.

The directors, Miriam Ekhator and Davidson Lynch-Shyllon, were disqualified from carrying on and/or managing or having a financial interest in a children's home.

They were also ordered to pay victim surcharges totalling Â£2,960, and costs of Â£17,250.

Musa Raji, on behalf of Catalyst Care Limited, said the defendants' "focus was on the children in front of them and sadly not on the paperwork", and they "made mistakes, but did not act out of malice or greed".

The prosecution said unregistered children's homes operate without oversight, meaning children who are placed there have no assurance of "safe or suitable care".

Ofsted say in such homes there are no guaranteed checks on staff or living conditions and there is no accountability when things go wrong.

But according to the regulator, the lack of available places in legitimate settings has led to a shadow market of illegal care homes.

News.title: Justice secretary apologises to families affected by early release scheme
News.content:
Justice Secretary Alex Norris has apologised to families affected by the early release scheme, saying they were "carrying the can from previous failures".

Families, including a man whose pregnant partner died after being hit by a speeding driver, criticised the prisoner early release scheme, saying it comes "at the expense of victims".

Andy Burnham announced that prisoners convicted of rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales. The prime minister said he wanted to exclude more, but prison overcrowding prevented this.

Calvin Buckley said he was "shocked and disappointed" the killer of his partner and unborn child could be released early.

The mother of PC Andrew Harper also said she was "devastated" to learn two men jailed after her son was killed will still be eligible.

The prime minister said making more prisoners exempt was not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".

Justice Secretary Alex Norris also warned a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris later said he spoke to the families as "it is really important to express that this shouldn't be where it is".

He also said he was confident the prisons would have adequate room now that about 1,000 extra prisoners will not be released early.

"We have modelled it very carefully," he said.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice confirming that two of the offenders could be included in the early release scheme.

While the driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter could apply for early release after serving half of their sentences.

The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.

The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.

But last month the prime minister promised to "review the policy" and paused the scheme after a backlash from survivors.

Announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."

But PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam, told BBC Newsnight: "It feels like we're letting Andrew down again" to hear his killers might still be eligible for release.

"We've been through the justice system, we thought we'd done as best as we could.

"Now we're standing up to fight again... so I just feel really let down, for Andrew's sake as well as ours."

She added that Norris had called her to explain the situation and apologise.

Later, on BBC Breakfast, Adlam called for more support from the probation service, stressing: "I need to know at the very, very least if they are going to be released that we're kept in mind of what's happening and we are informed".

Other families have also criticised the early release scheme.

Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough and unborn child died in May 2023.

"Our justice is being taken away, I understand there's a crisis, I agree that it needs to be addressed, but not at the expense of victims," he told BBC Breakfast.

News.title: Fires started 'deliberately' on mountain as crews tackle blaze
News.content:
She said the fire was particularly bad on Monday night when "the smoke was so thick I couldn't breathe" and added that the firefighters had been "amazing".

Ian Putland said even with the windows closed he could smell the fire.

"I heard about it a couple of days ago, and didn't think it would affect me... but then I came out yesterday and saw ash on the car and it indicated how close the fire was," he said.

"I was then alarmed with all the fire people about."

He added that he was "frustrated that the fires had been started deliberately".

"There's the wildlife killed, people are being put in danger and it takes emergency services away. It is a real waste of resources."

Christian Hadfield, area manager at SWFRS, said crews had been at the incident since Saturday but declared it a major incident on Monday in order to protect homes in the area.

"We are putting fire breaks in and monitoring the area," he said.

He added there were reports of "pockets of deliberate fire setting" which put the crews "under really critical conditions and stretches the service".

The fire was "unpredictable and complex work", he said, and firefighters could be there "for many days to come".

News.title: Scottish exam pass rates rise as students find out results
News.content:
Pass rates for Scottish exams have increased as students across the country received their results.

More than 148,000 learners have been finding out the results of their Nationals, Highers, Advanced Highers and Skills for Work Awards.

Qualifications Scotland - which replaced the Scottish Qualifications Authority last year after a number of controversies - said a record number of vocational and technical qualifications were awarded.

Figures show that the poverty-related attainment gap has narrowed compared with last year.

Admissions service Ucas said a record number of Scottish students aged 18 and under had been accepted into university or college. In total, 32,370 Scottish students of all ages secured places, up from 31,850 in 2025.

News.title: Breast cancer checks missing most women under 50 who are at risk, says study
News.content:
Breast cancer is a leading cause of death in women under 50 in the UK.

Most cases - 96% - are in women over 40, while 25% are in women over 75.

Men can get breast cancer too, with about 420 new cases every year in the UK.

Natasha Finch was diagnosed with an aggressive breast cancer at just 23 despite having no known risk factors.

She has since become an advocate for breast cancer awareness and wants young women to take symptoms seriously.

"I'm six years on and still here, still winning. Going to the GP was scary, but I'm so glad I went when I did â because if I hadn't, who knows?"

"I just want to advocate for girls."

This study, by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looks at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women.

They used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score.

If all women under 50 were to have this done, they estimate about a quarter (26.5%) would be categorised as at above-average risk and referred for further assessment.

This would include a third of women under 50 (34.8%) who develop breast cancer within 10 years.

By comparison, the current Nice criteria would result in 1.4% of women under 50 being referred for further assessment, which would include just 4.4% of those women who develop breast cancer.

A main reason for the disparity, the researchers say, is because three-quarters of women (73%) under 50 who develop breast cancer within a decade have no family history of breast cancer - the key criterion in the Nice guidelines.

News.title: Half-price rail travel extended to 18-year-olds
News.content:
Eighteen-year-olds will be able to buy half-price train tickets for most services when railcard rules are changed later this month, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

It's an extension of the 16-17 Saver railcard which currently expires when the holder turns 18. From 17 August, they will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase.

It means 17-year-olds will be able to buy the railcard up until the day before they turn 18, making it valid until the day before they turn 19.

Seventeen-year old Lily-Mae from Blackpool told the BBC the move would save her "a few hundred [pounds] a year".

She uses the train to travel regularly from Blackpool North to Preston and Manchester.

"I have been planning to see my boyfriend and my friends, and it's just not really happened because of the price of the trains," she said.

"Also getting to college for me is hard as I go to a college in Preston, but I live in a different town, so now I won't have to save as much money to get there."

The existing rule meant more than 70,000 students each year were an average of Â£175 worse off than those in the same academic year who hadn't yet had their 18th birthday, the DfT said.

The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs Â£35 per year and entitles the holder to 50% off most train fares.

Rail minister Lord Hendy claimed this "common sense change" is "exactly what passengers should expect from the railway".

He said the change would "lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they're pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market".

Jacqueline Starr, chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said the change demonstrates the sector's commitment to "offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway".

Kaynat Ahmad, vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the railcard as "essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training".

Eighteen-year-olds were already entitled to a 16-25 Railcard, but that only entitles them to a third off the cost of travel.

The government said the measure would be paid for through increased train ridership, with more passengers as a result of more people being able to access the discounted fares.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from Â£3 to Â£2 next year.

News.title: Man 'driven insane' by noise admits killing fish
News.content:
A man who admitted using motor oil and detergent to kill his neighbour's fish, after being "driven completely insane" by the noise of a water pump in the pond, has been sentenced.

Gerry Duffy, 76, of Hadley Road, Barnet, north London, pleaded guilty on the day of his trial at Willesden Magistrates' Court to three counts of damaging property and one count of unlawfully destroying fish in March.

The court heard Duffy climbed into Andreas Ptohides' garden to break the water pump "out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep", having warned his neighbour he would take matters into his own hands.

Duffy was given a two-year conditional discharge and ordered to pay Â£565 in compensation to his neighbour.

Duffy, who worked as a builder before his retirement, lives in a studio flat which backs on to the garden owned by his neighbour, the court heard.

Shahid Iftakhar, prosecuting, said the "neighbour dispute" between Duffy and Ptohides, potentially caused Â£565 of damage.

He said: "The defendant has previously complained to the complainant about noise coming from his garden and has said words to the effect of, 'if you didn't deal with it, I would' â there was a warning before the incident."

The prosecution added that Duffy was captured on CCTV having "climbed into the complainant's garden and damaged the water pipes and pumps".

In mitigation, Elliott Stern told the court his client had tried to deal with the dispute without resorting to killing the fish.

Mr Stern said: "The man has been driven completely insane by this noise, he's spoken to the complainant several times.

"They initially said they would stop the water pump going but then turned around and said that's not good for the fish."

An environmental officer came to the house and told Duffy he either had to "move or close his window", the court heard.

"Out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep, Mr Duffy, out of character, I would say, lost his mind and committed various damages," said Stern.

News.title: Tributes paid to 'quietly seismic' theatre director and playwright Peter Gill
News.content:
Theatre director, playwright and actor Peter Gill, who has died aged 86, has been described as a "gentle man with a fierce intelligence" who had a "quietly seismic" influence on British theatre.

Cardiff-born Gill performed with the Royal Shakespeare Company and appeared in films including HMS Defiant and Zulu before embarking on a successful theatre directing career.

Among those to pay tribute was Welsh actor Luke Evans, who credited Gill with launching his own career.

Gill's agent Mel Kenyon said his work had a "rare emotional delicacy" that was "beautifully observed and finely tuned".

Gill is closely associated with his work at the Royal Court in London, where he is credited with introducing the plays of English writer DH Lawrence to the theatrical world.

Born in Cardiff on 7 September 1939, he was raised in a working-class community and remained "fiercely proud of his Welsh heritage throughout his life", according to an obituary written by his agency Casarotto Ramsay & Associates.

He pursued an acting career from the age of 18 before moving into theatre, most closely associated with the Royal Court, where he championed three Lawrence plays A Collier's Friday Night, The Daughter-in-Law and The Widowing of Mrs Holroyd.

"Their success revived interest in Lawrence's dramatic work and helped spark a renaissance of his plays in London theatre circles after decades of relative obscurity following his death in 1930," the agency said.

He also presented two of his early plays, The Sleeper's Den and Over Gardens Out, at the theatre, before becoming associate director in 1970.

In 1976, he became artistic director of Riverside Studios, with his production of William Shakespeare's As You Like It marking the official opening of the Hammersmith-based theatre that year.

He also adapted Anton Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard for the theatre, helping transform it from a "small fringe theatre" into a "venue regarded as the equal of the leading theatres of the West End".

In 1980, he was appointed OBE for his services to theatre, also founding the National Theatre Studio in 1984 and running it until 1990.

News.title: Boy, 14, dies after going into water at dock
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has drowned after going into the water at a dock in east London.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) and the Metropolitan Police searched the Millwall Outer Dock near East Ferry Road after being alerted at about 18:50 BST on Monday.

His body was recovered at about 22:30 and he was pronounced dead at the scene. His family have been informed, police said.

In a post on social media, Mayor of Tower Hamlets Lutfur Rahman named the teenager as Banta Sillah and said he was "a talented young footballer who played for Frontline Community FC and was instrumental in helping the team win the Tower Hamlets Cup last week".

The Met Police has not confirmed the identity of the boy.

The mayor said Banta "had immense potential and was dearly loved by his peers".

He added: "As we mourn Banta, I urge families to speak with children and young people, we should all be aware of the dangers swimming in open water.

"Swimming should only take place in officially designated areas with lifeguards present."

News.title: Campaigners denied appeal over Gatwick expansion
News.content:
In a 29-page ruling, they said: "We conclude that each of the grounds of appeal raised by each appellant is unarguable.

"Neither appeal has a real prospect of success. We also consider that there are no other compelling reasons for either appeal to be heard."

The two senior judges also said that the previous ruling was "detailed and thorough".

Gatwick is the UK's second busiest airport and one of the busiest single-runway airports in the world.

The expansion will allow the site to be used for the departures of narrow-bodied planes such as Airbus A320s and Boeing 737s.

Following the decision, Barclay said: "We are very disappointed with the Court's decision. We took this challenge as far as we could because we believed that the decision to allow Gatwick to expand was fundamentally flawed.

"It was not supported by government policy, would only serve to line the pockets of the airport and airlines, and would do so at the expense of local residents and the climate."

Cagne said: "Residents should be immensely proud of what they have achieved in holding Gatwick Airport's shareholders to account.

"This proposed new runway will come at a significant cost to both the taxpayer and the planet."

News.content:

An erectile dysfunction drug may increase the risk of a common eye condition that can cause blindness.

Those taking the drug tadalafil long-term should have their eye health monitored, scientists warn.

Tadalafil, which is also used to tackle the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, works by relaxing muscles and increasing blood flow.

But the medication is also associated with causing various eye health issues, including conditions affecting the optic nerve and the macula – the part of the retina responsible for sharp detailed vision.

Researchers in Taiwan have discovered there is some suggestion the drug can increase the risk of glaucoma – the leading cause of blindness worldwide, which affects more than a million people in the UK.

Study authors stressed their findings “do not contraindicate tadalafil use” but highlight the importance of monitoring eye health, particularly among people with pre-existing glaucoma or a family history of the condition, as well as patients with high pressure inside the eye.

open image in gallery Researchers warned those taking the drug tadalafil long-term should have their eye health monitored ( PA )

For the study, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology, researchers studied data from 73,854 men aged at least 40 with a history of lower urinary tract symptoms.

Half had been prescribed tadalafil or another PDE5i for up to five years, and half were on other drugs.

Men were paired based on lifestyle factors that could influence health, including ethnicity, whether or not they smoked, and other underlying conditions such as diabetes or obesity.

Researchers analysed how likely both groups were to develop glaucoma and to start treatment after five years.

The study found that men on tadalafil were 22 per cent more likely to develop glaucoma and were 32 per cent more likely to develop ocular hypertension.

They were also 33 per cent more likely to develop primary open angle glaucoma – the most common type.

Because this was an observational study, no firm conclusions can be drawn from cause and effect, experts warn.

open image in gallery Glaucoma is usually detected during routine eye tests

Symptoms of glaucoma

Glaucoma typically produces no symptoms, leaving most people unaware that they have the condition, according to the NHS.

Because it develops gradually over many years, it is usually identified during routine eye tests.

The condition generally impacts both eyes, though symptoms can be more pronounced in one.

On occasion, glaucoma can manifest suddenly and present acute symptoms.

These include severe eye pain, a red eye, tenderness surrounding the eyes, blurred vision, rainbow-coloured circles around bright lights, feeling sick, vomiting, and a headache.

The NHS advises anyone with concerns about their vision to see their GP or an optician.

There is no link between receiving the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine before age 2 and being diagnosed with autism, according to a new study of more than 2.5 million U.S. children.

“These results reinforce existing evidence supporting the safety of MMR vaccination,” the medical research scientists, from University of Washington, wrote last week. The research supports decades of work with similar results, including by the World Health Organization, which said earlier this year there was no evidence that vaccines cause autism.

The results come at a fraught time for U.S. public health, and in particular for childhood vaccinations, including the MMR shot. Federal data reveals that MMR vaccination rates have been steadily dropping since before the pandemic and cases of life-threatening measles are at a 35-year high.

As measles outbreaks rage across the country, public officials’ messaging has been bewildering at times.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. - who promoted unapproved treatments for measles last year - told CNN this weekend that people should get the MMR vaccine to protect themselves against the virus. But Kennedy also questioned decades of findings regarding the safety of vaccines when talking about autism, losing his temper at CNN anchor Dana Bash over questions about his leadership and conversations with President Donald Trump.

open image in gallery Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. says the President Donald Trump wants the administration to look into any ties between vaccines and autism - despite decades of research showing there’s no link. A new study showing no ties between autism diagnoses and the measles vaccine builds on that evidence ( Getty )

“You are wrong when you say that this issue has been studied,” he told Bash.

Trump wants Kennedy to study any ties between autism and vaccines - despite current and established evidence.

The president previously suggested the combined MMR vaccine was “bad” and should be split up during a September press conference on autism.

“We want no mercury in the vaccine. We want no aluminum in the vaccine. The MMR I think should be taken separately. This is based on what I feel,” Trump said. “It seems to be that when you mix them, there could be a problem. So, there’s no downside in taking them separately. In fact, they think it’s better. So let it be separate.”

Kennedy has acknowledged studies have shown no link between the MMR vaccine and autism, according to The New York Times.

The MMR vaccine has been studied for decades around the world and is often mentioned when talking about autism because of a 1998 study by former doctor Andrew Wakefield that has since been disproven, according to the non-profit Autism Speaks.

The study in a small group of children suggested that vaccinations caused children's brain development to regress, but it was later retracted due to flawed methodology.

“Before it was retracted, Wakefield's 1998 study had been cited more than 600 times. This serves as an example of how easily misinformation can spread, and how hard it can be to correct,” the American Academy of Pediatrics says, noting that Wakefield’s medical license had been revoked.

open image in gallery A woman holds her young daughter while she gets the MMR vaccine at a clinic in Lubbock, Texas, last year. Kennedy said parents should give their children the shots on CNN this weekend ( Getty Images )

Kennedy’s remarks on the MMR vaccine and autism come less than a year after the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention updated its webpage on vaccines and autism.

The CDC page was changed in November to say studies “have not ruled out the possibility that infant vaccines cause autism” and studies supporting a link “have been ignored by health authorities.”

“HHS has launched a comprehensive assessment of the causes of autism, including investigations on plausible biologic mechanisms and potential causal links,” the CDC, which falls under Kennedy’s leadership, states.

“The whole thing about ‘vaccines have been tested and there’s been this determination made,’ is just a lie,” Kennedy told The Times last year, defending the move. “The phrase ‘Vaccines do not cause autism’ is not supported by science.”

That update drew alarm the academy, which blasted the move as a waste of government resources. “The American Academy of Pediatrics stands with members of the autism community who have asked for support in stopping this rumor from spreading any further,” President Dr. Susan Kressly said in a statement.

While many vaccines have not been individually tested for whether they might cause autism, it does not mean they haven’t been tested, the University of Pennsylvania’s Annenberg Public Policy Center’s FactCheck.org pointed out this week.

An England fan who prematurely crowned England as World Cup winners in a tattoo has had his new artwork amended.

Sean Carrington spent £550 on a leg tattoo of the World Cup trophy above the words "England World Cup Winner 2026" after The Three Lions’ 2-1 win over DR Congo in the round of 32.

The 36-year-old was so convinced Thomas Tuchel's side would go all the way before Argentina prematurely ended England’s chances of World Cup glory in a 2-1 defeat.

Now the roofer has returned to Holy Trinity Tattoo Studio in Standish to add “Just joking” underneath.

Following his second trip to the tattoo parlour, he told the BBC: "I'm more bothered that England hasn't won the World Cup than I am to have a tattoo on my leg”.

He added: "It's not bothering me. It's just a tattoo."

Carrington said he did not regret getting the original tattoo and he "wouldn't have done anything differently".

Sean Carrington does not regret his tattoo of the World Cup trophy above the words ‘England World Cup Winner 2026’ ( Social media )

He said he was happy with the result of the extra line added to his tattoo and remarked how it was "sound", adding: "I didn't really feel it."

Jamie Taylor, the parlour's manager, said the tattoo would normally have cost about £100, but they had decided to do the correction for free.

When asked whether he has plans for any more tattoos, Carrington did not rule out the possibility of getting another football-related tribute in the future.

"I don't plan any tattoo, it's just if it pops in my head," he said.

Holy Trinity Tattoo’s Facebook page shared a video of the new amendment which said: “This is exactly why tattoo artists tell you to wait.”

The venue added: “Well… this aged well.

“Last month our customer was so confident he had ‘England World Cup Winners 2026’ tattooed.

“Fast forward to today… and he’s been back for a little update.

“‘Just joking.’

“At least he’s got a good sense of humour! Fair play for owning it.”

After England’s late defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals, Tuchel’s side went on to finish the tournament in third place, beating France 6-4 in the ‘Bronze Final’ in Miami.

News.title: Man, 35, arrested on suspicion of murder after fatal shooting at traveller site
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder following a fatal shooting at a traveller site.

The suspect, 35, was arrested on Tuesday.

A total of five people have been arrested in connection to the incident, Wiltshire Police said.

The victim, who has been named by police as Jimmy Ward, 36, was declared dead at the scene near Cricklade, Wiltshire, at about 8.15am on Sunday.

Two other men, aged 53 and 29, were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender following a vehicle stop on the A419 road on Tuesday.

On Sunday, a 74-year-old man and 42-year-old woman were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender and possession of a firearm.

All five people are in custody for questioning, police confirmed.

Senior Investigating Officer Detective Chief Inspector Phil Walker said: “This is a significant development in our investigation.

“I can confirm that a man has been arrested on suspicion of Jimmy’s murder and is now in police custody, along with four other people on suspicion of assisting an offender.

“Jimmy’s next of kin have been informed of this development and my thoughts continue to be with them. They are being supported by specially trained officers.

“A scene and heavy policing presence remain in place at the traveller site in Calcutt while further inquiries are carried out. I continue to ask that this cordon is respected.

“I’d like to thank the local community for their support and patience since Sunday.

“We understand this incident has caused significant concern, so please consider speaking with officers about any information or concerns you may have.”

More to follow...

Turkish Super Lig club Trabzonspor say they have begun transfer discussions with Mohamed Salah.

The Egyptian is available on a free transfer after leaving Liverpool at the end of last season, and the club’s chairman said he hopes that a deal will be finalised later this week.

"Negotiations have been launched to transfer professional footballer Mohamed Salah, who is in a free status, to our club," the club said in a statement on Turkey's public disclosure platform.

Speaking to broadcaster A Spor shortly after the statement, Trabzonspor Chairman Ertugrul Dogan said that while the transfer was not yet complete, Salah was expected to arrive in Istanbul for medical checks on Wednesday and then head to Trabzon to sign with the Black Sea side.

He did not say when the contract would be signed, but said it would likely be on Thursday.

Salah left Liverpool this summer after nine years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, where he won the Premier League twice and the Champions League once.

In the 2024-25 season, Salah scored 29 Premier League goals and provided 18 assists, equalling the league record for most goal involvements in a single season and setting the record for a 38-game campaign.

Mohamed Salah celebrates scoring for Egypt at this summer’s World Cup ( Getty )

He was named Premier League Player of the Season and won the Golden Boot and the Playmaker Award, becoming the first player to take all three in one campaign.

His output waned last season, with seven goals and seven assists in 27 league matches and he was left on the bench in Champions League games, leading to a public spat with Liverpool's then-manager Arne Slot.

The 34-year-old started his career in Europe at Swiss side Basel in 2012 and later joined Chelsea. He also had brief stints at Fiorentina and AS Roma between 2015 and 2017 before joining Liverpool.

Trabzonspor – who are generally considered to be the fourth biggest team in Turkey after Istanbul sides Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, and Besiktas – finished third in the Super Lig last season and will enter the Europa League playoff round.

Salah had been close to joining Istanbul club Besiktas, whose football director Onder Ozen said negotiations had stalled over financial and image-rights demands, according to local media.
