Monsoon session is heading for a virtual washout as both Houses have been repeatedly adjourned since the session began except for a discussion on the bill making punishment in paper leak cases more stringent. RS witnessed an uproar as governing party and opposition had an angry exchange of words over the donation theft issue.

When LoP Malikarjun Kharge asked why govt agencies like ED, CBI and I-T were not probing the theft 'by members of Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra', parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju alleged that Congress and SP had always "abused Lord Ram" and "opposed Ram Temple construction."

World.title: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Dismissing reports of fuel quality issues at outlets, govt Tuesday said additional checks have been introduced by oil marketing companies (OMCs) to detect fuel contamination and adulteration.In a post on X, the petroleum ministry said OMCs were regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination, and that only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far."In addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing 8-12 times a day at over 87,000 outlets. Over 2,000 samples have also been tested for chloride/sulphide. Only two cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately," ministry said.It added that oil companies had been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination across the fuel supply chain, and strict action would be taken if contamination or adulteration was found at any retail outlet.Through a series of infographics on X, ministry said there was "zero compromise" on quality benchmarks and that 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026 for failing quality standards.It added that ethanol used for blending must comply with BIS IS 15464, have a minimum purity of 99.6% and be accompanied by a certified quality report. The ministry said ethanol is stored in dedicated facilities to prevent contamination, its quality is monitored regularly to ensure consistency and every tanker is sampled from both the top and bottom before being accepted.Separately, govt has so far approved Rs 4,687 crore as interest subsidy for eligible ethanol projects under its various support schemes, minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament Monday. Under the schemes, govt bears an interest subvention of 6% or 50% of the interest rate charged by lenders, whichever is lower, for five years on loans taken to set up new distilleries or expand existing ethanol production capacity.

World.title: Day after PK's poll win, PM Modi talks to Nabin, meets Nitish
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At an NDA parliamentary party meeting on Tuesday, govt representatives emphasised the big boost to employment generation and economic growth under PM Narendra Modi's leadership compared to the preceding UPA era, with India's "transformative journey" in sports also being highlighted.

Modi and home minister

were among those who attended the meeting, though the Prime Minister did not speak at the weekly gathering of governing alliance MPs.

A light-hearted conversation between Modi and

president Nitin Nabin during the closed-door meeting sparked talk in NDA circles, as many MPs interpreted it as the PM putting the Rajya Sabha member from Bihar at ease a day after BJP suffered a shock defeat in his pocket borough of Bankipur, which he had vacated after his election to Parliament.

Modi later also met former Bihar CM

, who was accompanied by his JDU colleagues Lalan Singh and Sanjay Jha, in his office. TNN

World.title: US Congressman warns FCRA Bill could affect India-US ties
World.content:
A US lawmaker on Tuesday criticised the amendments proposed to India's foreign funding law, alleging that they could allow the government to take over churches and religious charities and warning that the issue could affect India-US ties.

US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" and urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form.

In a post on X, the Republican Congressman from West Virginia said Christianity had a long history in India dating back to the arrival of St Thomas the Apostle on the Malabar Coast.

"But despite this long Christian history, India's Parliament is considering amending Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment (FCRA) rules to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities," Moore wrote.

"This is a clear attack against Christians. If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India," he added.

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes the creation of a Designated Authority that would take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such funds if an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or lapses after not being renewed.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





The Bill specifies that where such assets include a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is preserved.

It also proposes reducing the maximum punishment for violations of the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year.

The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable trusts, educational institutions, religious bodies and other associations. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.

Government data shows that as of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 had been cancelled and another 15,212 had expired.

World.title: From launch to data, tech to Isro facility, pvt firms to get 30-100% subsidy
World.content:
New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Indian private space companies and non-government entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to Isro facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).The incentives â Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme â being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031. The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India's position as a global launch hub.IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told TOI: âThe idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.âUnder Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities.The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too. âIt will be applicable to [Skyrootâs] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,â Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg. The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029. The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing Indiaâs space infrastructure, technologies and data.The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.

World.title: 6,868 medical camps, 18,000 surveillance teams deployed in Gujarat after floods
World.content:
The Gujarat health department has organised 6,868 medical camps, deployed more than 18,000 surveillance teams and administered preventive medicines to over 7.61 lakh people in flood-affected districts as part of an extensive drive to avert disease outbreaks following last week’s heavy rains, officials said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

According to officials, over 1.74 lakh people were examined and treated at the medical camps, while surveillance teams conducted daily door-to-door visits, distributing more than 1.05 crore chlorine tablets and 10.29 lakh ORS packets in affected areas.

The State government said a comprehensive Monsoon Action Plan had been implemented across all 34 districts and eight municipal corporations before and during the rainy season, helping prevent any major public health emergency despite widespread flooding.

Health authorities also conducted regular health check-ups in relief camps and shifted 675 pregnant women from vulnerable areas to healthcare facilities in advance, where 272 deliveries were carried out safely.

Round-the-clock health control rooms were established in all districts and municipal corporations, with each district receiving five additional emergency medical teams along with dedicated vehicles and staff. As many as 1,496 ambulances under the 108 Emergency Service and 816 ambulances attached to primary and community health centres have also been kept on standby.

The department said all government healthcare institutions have been stocked with more than 1.5 crore chlorine tablets, over 60 lakh ORS packets and 1,38,234 anti-snake venom injections.

Following the receding of floodwaters, preventive medicines against leptospirosis were administered to more than 7.61 lakh high-risk residents in 562 villages across Surat, Tapi, Valsad and Navsari districts. Additionally, 497 extra vector control teams were deployed in south and central Gujarat to undertake anti-larval measures and create public awareness against vector-borne diseases.

Torrential rain lashed several parts of south and central Gujarat on August 1, prompting authorities to evacuate around 27,000 people and rescue 53 others, particularly in Surat and Navsari districts, where flood-like conditions cut off several villages.

The India Meteorological Department has forecast light to moderate rainfall in parts of north, south and central Gujarat, as well as the Saurashtra region, during the week.

World.title: UCC panel invites ideas on proposed law in Chhattisgarh
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Chhattisgarh on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) announced that the committee formed to prepare the framework for the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) implementation in the State has invited suggestions and opinions on the proposed law from citizens, organisations and other stakeholders.

According to an official statement, the last date has been set as October 15 by the five five-member high-level committee. Last month, Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai had said that the UCC will be introduced in the Assembly in the upcoming Winter Session.

Since 2024, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh have implemented the UCC that largely regulates areas of personal law such as marriage, divorce, succession and inheritance, and live-in relationships.

“The committee is studying the legal, social and administrative aspects of implementing the UCC. Its mandate includes examining the State’s existing legal framework and preparing practical recommendations on matters such as marriage, divorce, maintenance, inheritance and adoption. It will also study UCC models adopted by other States, consider suggestions received from the citizens, legal experts, social organisations and other stakeholders, and prepare a comprehensive draft along with legislative and administrative recommendations,” the statement added.

The committee had appealed to government and non-government organisations, social groups, religious institutions, communities, political parties and citizens to submit their views and suggestions by October 15 this year, the statement said.

“Suggestions can be submitted by email at ucc-chhattisgarh@cg.gov.in, through the web portal https://ucc.cgstate.gov.in/, or by post to the Office of the Uniform Civil Code Committee, New Circuit House, Civil Lines, Room No. 202, Raipur, Chhattisgarh – 492001,” said the official.

While the government statement asserted that the objective of the proposed law was to bring all citizens under a common constitutional framework in place of religion-based personal laws, the Opposition has been long demanding that such a legislation proposed should provide exemptions for tribal communities. It demands that the centuries-old conservative traditions, marriage systems, and social systems of tribal communities should be excluded from the scope of the UCC to ensure that their specific rights are not violated.

In July, the Madhya Pradesh Assembly passed a UCC Bill with provisions to ban polygamy and make the registration of live-in relationships mandatory, while excluding the tribal community from its scope.

The committee headed by Justice Desai was examining the need for a Uniform Civil Code in Chhattisgarh, preparing its framework and undertaking a comprehensive review of the existing laws governing personal civil matters, the official added.

World.title: Flood in Assam due to Nagaland mining, will take up with Centre: Himanta Biswa Sarma
World.content:
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said he would discuss with the Centre the issue of mining in Nagaland as one of the causes of the devastating flood that has killed 87 people so far.

A majority of the people died in three districts adjoining Nagaland — Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat. These districts hardly have a history of a major flood.

Touring the flood-hit districts, Mr. Sarma said the State government will begin assessing the damage to the houses from August 9 to fast-track relief and rehabilitation of the affected families.

He also addressed concerns about mining activities in Nagaland having contributed to the unprecedented flooding in the three districts, specifically Charaideo and Sivasagar. “I cannot stop mining in Nagaland. I will raise the issue with the Centre. We need a scientific study to determine the actual cause of the problem,” he said, insisting there was no illegal mining in Assam.

Many in the affected districts, including Sibsagar MLA Akhil Gogoi, have blamed illegal sand, stone, and coal mining along the foothills of Nagaland for the flood in Assam. They said such activities, along with rampant felling of trees, removed natural resistance to the floodwaters that rushed down the hills of Nagaland after bouts of extremely heavy rain.

Nagaland-based organisations, however, trashed “theories” that activities there were responsible for Assam’s flood.

Mr. Sarma said the government would drain out the floodwaters as quickly as possible, apart from rebuilding the houses under the government’s rehabilitation programme.

He said the highways obstructed the natural flow of floodwater in certain areas. “I will ask the National Highways Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited to construct additional cross-drainage structures,” he said.

He further said embankments would be constructed in vulnerable areas to prevent flood damage in future.

Higher compensation

Mr. Sarma concurred with Mr. Gogoi’s suggestion that the compensation to flood victims should be increased.

Donations have been pouring in from individuals, organisations, political parties, and social media influencers.

Many have touched hearts with ‘shram daan’ or voluntary labour. They include a group of Sikhs who have been cleaning up flooded namghars (prayer halls), temples, and other places of worship besides serving meals.

A group of daily wagers from western Assam, mostly Bengali Muslims and Koch-Rajbongshis, has been clearing silt from farmlands and house compounds, or removing livestock carcasses.

Members of a barbers’ association have been providing free haircuts to the flood-affected people. At the same time, car mechanics from other parts of Assam have pitched in to repair vehicles free of charge. “Visuals of hundreds of upturned, half-buried two-, three-, and four-wheelers made us reach out to the people. We do not have cash to spare, but decided we can make a difference by trying to restore these vehicles without any labour charge,” a mechanic from Nagaon said.

World.title: Hexavalent vaccine could improve India’s immunisation programme: Study
World.content:
Introducing the hexavalent (six-in-one) vaccine into India’s Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) could improve the efficiency of the country’s childhood immunisation programme, according to a study conducted by the Union Health Ministry along with the George Institute for Global Health India, the Gates Foundation, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and John Snow India Private Limited.

A hexavalent (six-in-one) vaccine is a combination vaccine that protects infants against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (whooping cough), Hepatitis B, Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and polio in a single injection. It reduces the number of injections children need, eases the workload of frontline health workers, lowers cold-chain requirements, and saves caregivers’ time.

According to a release issued by the group, almost 26 million Indian babies are vaccinated annually as part of the nation’s immunisation programme. At present, children receive multiple vaccines during immunisation visits, increasing the number of injections they receive, placing additional demands on caregivers’ time, and adding to the workload of healthcare providers.

Researchers found that the price of the hexavalent vaccine remains the single largest determinant of overall programme costs. Based on trends in vaccine procurement in India, the study estimates that a 50% reduction in the vaccine price would enable operational and system-level savings to outweigh the additional vaccine acquisition costs under the primary immunisation schedule.

The research shows that introducing the hexavalent vaccine could deliver several benefits, including fewer injections for infants, making vaccination more convenient for children and caregivers.

The study assessed two implementation scenarios: replacing the current pentavalent and fractional IPV doses with the hexavalent vaccine during the primary immunisation schedule, and replacing both the primary schedule and the DTP booster dose with the hexavalent booster. Costs were assessed from both government and household perspectives, including vaccine procurement, syringes, cold-chain logistics, healthcare worker time, and caregiver time.

The findings were published in the peer-reviewed international journal *Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics*. Previous stakeholder research cited by the authors found that caregivers generally preferred fewer injectable vaccines during each visit.

Susmita Chatterjee, Program Head, Health Economics, the George Institute for Global Health India, said, “Combination vaccines have long been recognised for simplifying immunisation programmes while improving convenience for families and health systems. Our study demonstrates that although the hexavalent vaccine carries a higher upfront procurement cost, it also generates important efficiencies by reducing injections, easing pressure on frontline health workers, lowering cold-chain requirements and saving caregivers’ time. These findings provide important economic evidence that can inform future policy discussions on strengthening India’s immunisation programme.”

World.title: Sense of insecurity emerges as key concern of elderly people during panel’s sitting in Kochi
World.content:
A sense of insecurity and lack of support system faced by the elderly population emerged as a predominant concern during a sitting held by the Kerala State Elderly Commission (KSEC) at the district collectorate here on Tuesday.

The complaints lodged by senior citizens with the Commission pertained to a variety of issues including alleged neglect of elderly parents by adult children, financial cheating, and trouble from neighbours, officials said.

The Commission received seven complaints during the sitting, five from individuals and two from organisations involved in issues of the elder community.

“A common complaint we receive is about the alleged neglect of parents by children after getting their properties transferred to the latter’s name. Today also there were a couple of such complaints. There were also complaints about troubles from neighbours, including an allegation that improper maintenance of pets in neighbourhood was causing health issues to the complainant,” KSEC Chairperson K. Somaprasad said.

He added that the complainants approached the Commission alleging inaction by the authorities they had approached earlier. One of the complaints was from a retired government employee who had accused a non-banking financial company based in Aluva of cheating him of ₹85 lakh by promising higher returns on investment. The complainant knocked on the Commission’s door alleging that the local police were not keen to investigate the complaint.

A similar complaint alleged that a lender was not returning a 1.25-acre property mortgaged by an elderly person despite repaying the private loan.

Mr. Somaprasad said the Commission would seek report from the departments or agencies concerned on the complaints and summon the parties involved for hearing accordingly. Though two complaints received earlier were scheduled to be heard on Tuesday, neither of the opposing parties in one case turned up. Only the complainant appeared before the panel in the second case.

The Commission is scheduled to conduct similar hearing in other districts in the coming days. It has received around 300 complaints from across the State in the past nine months and nearly 50 of them have been disposed of.

World.title: Are pellet guns legal for crowd control in India? | Explained
World.content:
Story so far: At least one of the 80 protesters injured in police action during the Monday (July 20, 2026) march to Parliament called by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) sustained pellet gun injuries, according to a source at Lady Hardinge Medical College, where the victim is undergoing treatment. While the Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns and said such claims are “false and misleading”, the allegations have been strong against the Rapid Action Force, a specialised rapid reaction wing of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). This prompts questions over the legal framework governing the use of pellet guns and non-lethal weapons for crowd control in India.

The use of ‘non-lethal’ pellet guns was widely criticised during the 2024 farmers’ protests. Though the police denied using pellet guns, farmer leaders had alleged that several people were injured. They were also used in Manipur in 2023 and in Kashmir since 2010.

World.title: New seahorse species identified by Kerala researchers
World.content:
Marine researchers claimed to have solved a 150-year-old taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of the thorny seahorse, Hippocampus histrix.

Scientific studies have identified a new species, Hippocampus amandavincentae, which was previously misidentified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.

Earlier, researchers had described Hippocampus jayakari, a lesser-known one, which was also previously wrongly identified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.

The new species, which was named after noted marine biologist Amanda Vincent, was collected from the fish bycatch at the Tuticorin fisheries harbour by Shalu Kannan, the lead author of the paper.

The species was described in a recently released research paper, according to the team of researchers from Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos).

This is also the fifth known seahorse species from the Kerala coast, they said.

The study published in the taxonomy journal Zootaxa demonstrated that the thorny seahorse (Hippocampus histrix), historically believed to be widespread from the Red Sea and East Africa across the Indian Ocean to the western Pacific, was three distinct species, they claimed.

“Many museum specimens and online biodiversity records of spiny seahorses in the Indian Ocean have been assigned to Hippocampus histrix for decades,“ said Rajeev Raghavan, Assistant Professor at Kufos and a senior author of the study.

The new species was photographed alive during a survey held as part of the Ecomarine project at around 15-metre depth on the rocky reefs off Anchuthengu, said Kufos Vice-Chancellor A. Biju Kumar.

World.title: Security beefed up as Congress, PDP, NC to observe August 5 as 'Black Day'
World.content:
Security has been intensified across the Jammu region, particularly along the Jammu-Srinagar and Jammu-Pathankot national highways, as the National Conference (NC), the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the Congress have announced separate protests to observe August 5 as ‘Black Day’.

August 5 marks the seventh anniversary of the Centre's decision to abrogate the special status of the erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir State under Article 370 and reorganise it into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

Police, the Army and the CRPF have stepped up security arrangements by increasing vehicle checking, frisking and surveillance at sensitive locations across the region, officials said.

Special checkpoints have been placed on high alert along the Jammu-Srinagar and Jammu-Pathankot highways, with security personnel conducting searches of vehicles and verifying the identity of commuters, they said.

Security has also been strengthened in border areas, where patrolling and area domination exercises have been intensified as a precautionary measure, the officials said, adding that additional deployments have been made at vulnerable locations.

The National Conference leadership will assemble outside the party headquarters in Jammu and stage a protest on Wednesday, party leaders said.

The Congress will hold a demonstration outside its Shaheedi Chowk headquarters, demanding restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir, along with constitutional safeguards for land, jobs and natural resources, party leaders said.

The PDP will also hold a protest at its Gandhi Nagar headquarters to mark the occasion, its leaders said.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs3.39, high-speed diesel by Rs4.07
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.39 and Rs4.07 per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs328.56 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs385.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for August 5 (Wednesday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Qatar says progress made toward US-Iran talks on ending war
World.content:
Qatar said mediators were making progress in efforts to end the US-Iran war on Tuesday, driving oil prices lower, although Tehran has denied President Donald Trump’s assertion that talks are already under way.

Benchmark Brent crude fell more than four per cent after the comments from Qatar, extending Monday’s steep losses on hopes that an arrangement could soon be reached to restore traffic through the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. But for now, the strait remained virtually shut, with another ship reportedly coming under attack while trying to cross it.

Trump said on Monday that talks with Tehran had started and Iran faced a “last chance” to reach a deal. Iranian officials insisted no negotiations with the United States were taking place. Iran says its only talks are with Oman about the strait, and that no major meetings were planned this week.

But senior US officials struck an optimistic tone on Tuesday, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both pointing to progress in discussions aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a corridor that normally carries about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.

“There’s been progress made in those talks, but not finality yet. We’re hoping that will happen very shortly,” Rubio told reporters at the State Department.

Bessent said a deal with Iran on the reopening of Hormuz could be reached by Tuesday or Wednesday. Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said diplomatic contacts had reached “very progressive stages”.

He said mediators including Qatar, Pakistan and Oman were coordinating closely to facilitate negotiations and exchange draft proposals between Washington and Tehran.

Trump’s comments followed his weekend decision to cancel what he described as “massive attacks” on Iran, extending a pattern in which he has threatened major military action before later backing off and pointing to diplomatic contacts.

Shipping risks remain

Iran has halted most traffic through Hormuz while Washington maintains a blockade of Iran-related shipping and ports. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have also imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, further restricting oil export routes.

A cargo vessel reported being struck by an unidentified projectile near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman’s coast, according to the UKMTO maritime security agency. Maritime sources told Reuters on Tuesday that the vessel was a dry bulk ship. Its crew had to abandon the vessel and one seafarer was missing.

Iran has long demanded control over the strait, which it says it should share with Oman, which controls the opposite shore. Tehran rejected an Omani proposal last week that would have allowed shared oversight of the strait and the collection of voluntary fees from ships. A senior Iranian source said Iran is seeking full control over inbound shipping through the strait, and visibility over outbound traffic, with the ability to intervene if necessary.

Giving Iran such control would be a major shift in the regional balance of power and make it more difficult for Washington to argue that “Operation Epic Fury”, which Trump launched alongside Israel in February, had weakened Washington’s longstanding foe.

Questions are also growing about the sustainability of the US military campaign. The US Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during the war, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military’s readiness for future conflicts.

Prolonged pain

Gulf officials and analysts say Iran is betting it can outlast Washington by turning the region’s trade routes, shipping lanes and energy infrastructure into pressure points that steadily raise the cost of confrontation.

“Their big advantage is that they can hurt the regional states and the global economy,” said Michael Knights of the Washington Institute.

Iran has publicly rejected negotiations with Washington since the collapse in early July of a memorandum of understanding the two sides signed the previous month in an attempt to end the conflict.

Trump has yet to achieve the objectives he set out at the start of the war: dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme, curbing its ability to attack regional rivals and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.

World.title: AJK elections: PPP, IPP ahead in two Muzaffarabad constituencies
World.content:
ISLAMABAD/ MUZAFFARABAD: The PPP and Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) appeared set to win the two constituencies in Muzaffarabad division where polling had been postponed due to landslides and bad weather.

Voting was held in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kotla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) after authorities delayed the exercise due to blocked roads.

According to unofficial results, PPP’s Syed Bazil Ali Naqvi retained LA-28 (Lachhrat), defeating Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) candidate Chaudhry Shahzad Mehmood.

Polling was held at 122 of the constituency’s 174 polling stations on Sunday. However, following allegations that PPP workers had taken away ballot boxes, the Election Commission ordered repolling at two of those stations, along with polling at the remaining 52 stations where voting could not be held earlier.

Results from the remaining 120 polling stations had put Naqvi ahead of his rival by just five votes.

Meanwhile, polling was held at all 197 polling stations in LA-27 (Kutla), where voting had been postponed entirely until Tuesday.

According to preliminary and unofficial results from 115 polling stations, IPP’s Sardar Tabarak Ali was leading with 15,770 votes, followed by PML-N’s Noreen Arif with 12,800 votes and PPP’s Sardar Javed Ayoub with 9,880 votes.

Naqvi’s victory took the PPP’s tally in the Muzaffarabad division to four seats, bringing it level with the PML-N’s strength in the division. Ali, meanwhile, was set to secure the first Assembly seat for the nascent IPP, whose regional president, Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, had polled just 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases due to security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division on August 10.

The first phase of polling was held in AJK’s Mirpur division on July 27, in which the PML-N had secured nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four.

The two parties, which are allies in Centre, have been engaged in a war of words since, with the PPP accusing the PML-N of rigging, violence and electoral malpractices.

Rigging allegations

It levelled the same allegations on Tuesday, with the party posting a complaint on its X account that it said it had sent to the Election Commission.

It claimed that polling staff had been “caught red-handed with official ballot papers and polling bags inside the house of a PML-N supporter, approximately two kilometres from the designated polling site” in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kotla) in union council Bheri.

The PPP claimed it had “concrete evidence” that polling staff at polling station no.3 had moved to the residence of a PML-N candidate and abandoned their post.

It also shared a statement by PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman on X, with her saying that and the reports of the presence of polling staff at a PML-N supporter’s residence were concerning.

She said videos related to “rigging by the PML-N” had been handed over to the Election Commission as evidence and demanded immediate disciplinary and legal action.

When Dawn asked Election Commission official Khawaja Muhammed Ahsan about the videos, he said a PPP worker had shared some videos, but “they are vague and amount to a little more than unverified allegations”.

“Unless the footage is authenticated through proper forensic examination and corroborated by other credible evidence, it cannot be treated as proof,” he added.

Meanwhile, the PPP shared another complaint addressed to the Election Commission on X. It accused the PML-N of ballot stuffing at polling stations no.95 and no.97 in LA-28 and of obstructing the polling process by barring voters from casting their votes.

The PPP also alleged that at polling station no.92 in LA-27, the presiding officer was stuffing ballots and called for him to be replaced by someone “neutral”.

In yet another complaint, the PPP accused PML-N workers of firing in Bandi in LA-28 to “terrorise the residents of Bandi and keep them inside their homes so that they do not proceed to the polling stations”.

Later in the evening, the PPP Azad Kashmir election cell also submitted video evidence of alleged fake voting at polling station No. 92 in the Municipal Committee Pateeka area, in constituency LA-27 Muzaffarabad-1 (Kotla), to the election commission and demanded immediate action.

In a complaint filed by PPP election cell incharge Javed Ayub, the party alleged that the polling station had been turned into a “factory for fake votes”, claiming that PML-N workers openly cast fake votes throughout the day.

It further alleged that the presiding officer failed to perform his duties and that ballot papers were stamped in his absence. The PPP said it had submitted video evidence and other material to the election commission and called for action against those responsible for alleged violations of electoral laws.

Tallal Chaudhry tells Bilawal to ’show grace in defeat’

Meanwhile, Minister of State for Interior and PML-N’s election coordinator for Poonch division, Tallal Chaudhry, rejected earlier allegations of rigging made by PPP in the AJK elections and took a swipe at PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, saying “leaders should not cry over defeat”, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry.

Presiding over a review meeting on the third phase of AJK elections in Poonch division, Chaudhry said PML-N’s sweeping victory in the first two phases was a reflection of public trust in the performance of the federal and Punjab governments.

“The people of Kashmir have voted for work and performance,” he told district constituency coordinators and PML-N candidates from Poonch division who attended the meeting.

Seemingly responding to PPP’s allegations related to electoral malpractices, the minister said: “Bilawal Bhutto should show a big heart. Leaders do not look good when they cry over defeat.”

He added that the mandate given to PML-N in AJK showed that “every part of Pakistan wants to become like Punjab” in terms of development and governance.

He expressed confidence that the PML-N would secure a majority of seats in the third phase of the AJK elections.

A day earlier, Bilawal had warned the PML-N that a “countdown” for it had begun and declared that his party’s “movement” for people’s rights would extend to the entire country.

In a series of clips posted on X on Monday, Bilawal affirmed that his party’s struggle for the people’s right to governance, ownership and employment will continue.

The PPP chairman said, “And my message for the friends in PML-N is just this: you can hear that voice, listen carefully, tick tock, tick tock. Your countdown has begun.”

Bilawal had given a similar warning last week to the federal government, which is led by the PML-N in alliance with his own PPP.

World.title: Dar departs for ministerial meeting in Jordan on deteriorating situation in occupied Jerusalem: FO
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar departed for a one-day visit to Jordan on Tuesday to attend a ministerial meeting aimed at formulating a unified position on the situation in occupied Jerusalem, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The FO posted on X that the foreign minister had left for Amman, Jordan, where he would “reaffirm Pakistan’s unwavering support for the Palestinian people and their just cause”.

The Ministerial Meeting on Jerusalem, scheduled to be held on Aug 5 (Wednesday), will bring together foreign ministers from Arab League member states and a group of Islamic countries to discuss the deteriorating situation in the region, the FO said in a previous statement shared on social media.

Dar was invited to attend by Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Al Safadi, the statement said.

“The attending foreign ministers will also call on His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein, King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, during the visit,” the FO added.

The foreign minister is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting to exchange views on regional developments, including the humanitarian situation in Palestine.

The FO termed Dar’s participation in the meeting “a manifestation of Pakistan’s principled support for the Palestinian people” and its commitment to the establishment of an “independent, sovereign and contiguous” State of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

Pakistan and other Muslim countries have repeatedly condemned “continued incursions by extremist Israeli settlers” into Al Aqsa Mosque — Islam’s third-holiest site, located in east Jerusalem, which Israel captured in 1967 and later annexed.

The Al-Aqsa compound is a central symbol of Palestinian identity and also a frequent flashpoint. Under long-standing arrangements, Jewish people may visit the compound, but are not permitted to pray there. While Israel says it is committed to maintaining this status quo, Palestinians fear it is being eroded.

The foreign ministers of Pakistan and eight other Muslim countries in June expressed their “categorical rejection” of any attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites.

World.title: Cop allegedly rapes woman inside Lahore police station; entire staff suspended
World.content:
LAHORE: The entire staff of Lahore’s Ghaziabad police station was suspended on Tuesday after it emerged that an assistant sub-inspector had allegedly raped a woman on the premises on Sunday.

Lahore DIG (Operations) Faisal Kamran confirmed the development to Dawn, saying that the woman was allegedly raped by an assistant sub-inspector inside a room at the police station.

He said the woman had identified, in the presence of senior police officials, the exact room where she was allegedly raped. “The room was located on the upper floor of the police station,” he said.

The DIG said he suspended the entire staff of the police station because, according to police rules, all of them were responsible for keeping a check on any wrongdoing at the station.

“No one bothered to enquire why the ASI had brought the woman to the police station in the absence of any female personnel,” he said.

Over 70 personnel and officials deployed at the police station have been suspended, according to a police report seen by Dawn.

A first information report (FIR) of the incident, a copy of which is available with Dawn, was registered at Ghaziabad police station on Monday under Section 376 (punishment for rape) of the Pakistan Penal Code and 155-C of Police Order, 2002, which outlines penalties for misconduct by police officers.

The FIR quotes the complainant, the woman’s father, as saying that his daughter, aged around 20 and mentally impaired, had left home in the afternoon on Sunday and did not return for a long time, following which they began searching for her.

He said a man told him that a policeman, who was in civilian clothes, had taken his daughter away with him.

“We then reached the Ghaziabad police station at around 9pm. But as soon as we reached there, my brother called and told me that my daughter had returned home,” he told police, adding that his daughter was crying when he reached home.

When asked for the reason, she said a police official had taken her with him on a motorcycle and then raped her.

Prosecutor general takes notice

Punjab Prosecutor General Irfan Sadiq Tarar has taken notice of the incident, declaring it a high-profile case and directing that the investigation be conducted in a transparent, impartial and merit-based manner.

According to a statement, Tarar has summoned the investigating officer to his office on Thursday, along with the complete case record for a review of the investigation.

He directed that all stages of the probe be completed in accordance with the law, warning that any negligence or delay would not be tolerated.

The prosecutor general also said ensuring legal protection and justice for the survivor was the prosecution department’s top priority, adding that crimes against women and children were intolerable and would be prosecuted effectively on the basis of strong evidence so that those responsible could be punished in accordance with the law.

World.title: Transporters demand lower taxes and diesel prices, threaten wheel-jam strike from Aug 8
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The All Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance on Tuesday announced a nationwide wheel-jam strike from Aug 8, warning that the suspension of freight movement could disrupt the supply of essential commodities if the government failed to address its demands.

The announcement was made at a press conference at the National Press Club by the alliance’s leaders, including All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate, Malik Shafeeullah Awan and Malik Nisar.

They said the transport sector was facing an unprecedented financial crisis due to repeated increases in diesel prices, higher taxes and other government measures. The transporters demanded that taxes on diesel be reduced and fuel prices be restored to their July 1, 2024, level.

Demands were also issued for a reduction in the withholding tax on cargo transporters from seven per cent to 2pc, arguing that oil tanker operators were already paying only 2pc.

The alliance also rejected a provision introduced in the Finance Act 2026 under which an entire vehicle could be confiscated if non-duty-paid goods were found on board.

Describing the measure as unjust and demanding its immediate withdrawal, the transporters urged the government to restore the previous system under which fines were imposed and vehicles released.

They also sought uniform implementation of axle-load regulations across the country, saying overloading should be checked at factories, warehouses and loading points rather than through roadside enforcement, which they alleged had become a source of revenue collection.

Among other demands, the transporters called for a simpler procedure for obtaining heavy transport vehicle driving licences, a reduction in toll taxes and an end to the daily adjustment of diesel prices. They demanded that fuel prices be revised fortnightly or monthly to provide greater certainty for transport operators.

All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry said the current policies had pushed drivers, small transporters and vehicle owners paying instalments on financed trucks into severe financial hardship, making it increasingly difficult for them to continue operations.

“We have repeatedly approached the government through letters, meetings and media appeals, but no meaningful progress has been made,” he said.

It was jointly announced that unless the government entered into immediate negotiations and accepted their demands, all categories of goods transport, including cargo trucks, containers and oil tankers, would remain off the roads from Aug 8.

The alliance leaders said the strike would remain peaceful, adding that transporters would park their vehicles instead of blocking highways.

However, Malik Nisar warned that a prolonged shutdown could significantly affect imports, exports and the transportation of essential goods, adding that the government would bear responsibility for the consequences.

World.title: All foreign media personnel to require NOC from info ministry for news coverage outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi
World.content:
All foreign media personnel will now require a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MOIB) to travel to any city outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi for news coverage, according to recently issued guidelines.

The new Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines, 2026, outline requirements for the registration and accreditation of “foreign media houses, organisations and outlets working in Pakistan and all eligible journalists, media owners, media professionals, sources, freelancers, sponsors, fixers, attached persons, assignees etc, of Pakistan working or contributing for them”.

All foreign media personnel already accredited or registered with the MOIB’s External Publicity (EP) Wing will require a mandatory NOC from the wing for movement to any city except Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi, in order to produce “news content, story, video, film, documentary or social media content” for official use.

For leisure trips to Abbottabad and Murree, a NOC may be granted by the EP Wing upon the request of the journalist, within three working days, the notification added.

The guidelines apply to all foreign or international print, electronic and digital media, including social media and web-based platforms.

According to the new guidelines, all journalists working with international or foreign media outlets must register with the EP Wing through a designated Online Registration and Accreditation portal available at www.dml.nimar.pk/www.registration.epwing.gov.pk.

“All Pakistani journalists residing abroad, contributing to foreign media and seeking registration must submit their application through the EP Wing portal and concurrently forward their case through the nearest press attaché, counsellor, minister posted in Pakistan missions, consulates, high commissions, or embassies,” the MOIB said.

Additionally, all companies, entities, production houses etc. operating in Pakistan to facilitate foreign media “in any capacity” are also required to register with the ministry’s publicity wing, as are non-journalists living in Pakistan who render services to foreign media.

“Registration shall not confer any official status and only establishes professional recognition,” the notification pointed out, adding that registration would only be considered if supported by a recommendation from the head of the organisation.

After registration, journalists seeking a Press Accreditation Card must submit their request via the portal alongside required documents. There are two types of accreditation: permanent accreditation to be granted on an annual basis, and temporary accreditation for visiting journalists, valid for a maximum of three months.

Upon issuance of the EP Wing’s accreditation card, the wing will “facilitate” the journalists’ access to all official media events and government premises. Journalists will be “bound to produce that card on demand” and the card must be surrendered upon change of category or organisation, or upon the completion of the accreditation tenure.

The notification said that registration cards may be issued within seven working days from the submission of an application, while the accreditation card may take four to six weeks. The MOIB may seek additional information and documents if required, it added.

World.title: Palestinians mourn 112 people retrieved from rubble in Gaza
World.content:
Palestinians in Gaza held funeral prayers on Tuesday for 112 people recovered from under the rubble of homes destroyed during Israel’s war on the enclave.

The funeral is considered one of the largest in Palestinian history due to the high number of victims.

Thousands of Palestinians took part in the funeral in Gaza City’s Sabra neighbourhood, where the bodies were draped in Palestinian flags and placed near the ruins of the destroyed homes, according to an Anadolu reporter.

The victims were members of the Al-Hasayneh and Abu Sharia families, who were killed when the Israeli army bombed their homes while they were inside on November 23, 2023. They are set to be buried at the Baptist Cemetery in the Zeitoun neighbourhood, south of Gaza City, after the funeral procession.

The bodies were retrieved from the rubble by civil defence teams on Saturday.

“The victims included 40 children, 38 women and seven people with disabilities,” it said in a statement.

“The teams were unable to find 157 bodies still missing under the rubble,” Civil Defence official Mohammad Abu Dan added.

Israel has killed more than 73,000 people and injured over 174,000 others in a brutal war in Gaza since October 2023.

Despite the ceasefire agreement in effect since October 10, 2025, Israel has continued its attacks across the enclave, killing 1,250 Palestinians and injuring 4,110 others, according to Gaza’s health ministry.

​​​​​​​Palestinian authorities in Gaza estimate that around 9,500 people remain under the rubble of buildings destroyed by Israel across Gaza.

World.title: 53 cultural properties damaged by Kumamoto quake
World.content:
The 7.1-magnitude earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture last week had affected 53 cultural properties, including those at World Heritage sites, as of Monday, the Cultural Affairs Agency said.

The affected assets, located in Kumamoto and neighboring Fukuoka, Nagasaki and Kagoshima prefectures, include three national treasures and 11 national important cultural properties.

Of the total, 48 affected properties are in Kumamoto Prefecture.

At Shohinken, a centuries-old tea house with a garden in the city of Yatsushiro that is a national scenic site, a building collapsed, windows shattered and the pond water level temporarily fell.

The main building of the former Iseri family residence, a national registered tangible cultural property also known as a sake brewery, in the town of Hikawa, is now severely tilted.

Kumamoto Castle in the city of Kumamoto was battered by the earthquake amid restoration efforts following twin powerful quakes a decade ago. The stone walls of the symbol of the prefecture collapsed in dozens of places, and the main tower was cracked. The scheduled full reopening in fiscal 2052 may be delayed.

Of World Heritage sites related to the Meiji industrial revolution, windows broke at Misumi West Port in the city of Uki and Manda Pit in the city of Arao.

Some buildings of Aoi Aso Shrine in the city of Hitoyoshi and Tsujunkyo Bridge in the town of Yamato, both designated as national treasures, were partly damaged.

World.title: Toyota raises full-year net profit forecast
World.content:
Toyota on Tuesday revised up its full-year net profit forecast from ¥3 trillion to ¥3.25 trillion, reflecting the yen’s further weakening, as well as progress in securing alternative export routes to the Middle East.

The revised figure is still down 15.5% from the previous year’s result due to the fallout from tensions in the Middle East.

For fiscal 2026, which ends next March, the leading Japanese automaker also upgraded its operating profit projection from ¥3 trillion to ¥3.4 trillion, down 9.7% from the previous year.

The weaker yen helped improve the profit projection by ¥480 billion, and the impact of declining exports and rising material prices due to the Middle East situation was estimated to be ¥160 billion lower, at ¥510 billion.

Considering the yen’s recent movements, Toyota revised its assumed foreign exchange rates to ¥160 per dollar and ¥181 per euro.

Toyota’s annual revenue forecast was raised from ¥51 trillion to ¥54 trillion, up 6.5% from the previous year. Its projection for global vehicle sales, including those at subsidiary Daihatsu, was kept unchanged at 11.18 million units, as a higher projection for sales in North America, where sales of hybrid vehicles are robust, offset a weaker projection in Asia.

The latest projections did not reflect the impact of the suspension of production at some plants following a powerful earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture last week, as the company is scrutinizing the impact.

In April-June, the company’s consolidated net profit jumped 75.6% from a year before to ¥1.477 trillion, the first increase for the quarter in two years, on the back of a weaker-than-expected yen.

Meanwhile, quarterly operating profit declined 8.8% to ¥1.063 trillion. Revenues rose 10.4% to ¥13.525 trillion.

Global vehicle sales decreased 4.1% to 2,714,000 units, as sales in the Middle East decreased.

World.title: Takaichi urged BOJ chief to buy JGBs at May meeting
World.content:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda at their meeting in May to buy Japanese government bonds if necessary to curb rising long-term interest rates, informed sources said Tuesday.

It is unusual for the prime minister to mention a specific monetary policy tool. The reported request could spark a debate over the central bank’s independence.

According to the sources, Takaichi told Ueda during their 20-minute meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office on May 22 that she would like the BOJ to understand her Cabinet’s policy agenda and conduct appropriate monetary policy accordingly.

At a time when the BOJ is reducing its JGB purchases, the prime minister sought an appropriate response to ensure market stability, asking the central bank to buy JGBs if necessary.

Ueda replied that it is necessary to consider market reactions and added that the central bank would respond if circumstances warranted doing so, the sources said.

A government source said that Takaichi’s request reflected her hope to avoid a rise in long-term interest rates that could result from a possible increase in government bond issuance to finance crisis preparedness investments and higher defense spending under her “responsible and proactive” fiscal policy.

About three weeks after the Takaichi-Ueda meeting, the BOJ decided on June 16 to raise its policy interest rate to 1% and stop reducing its JGB purchases in April 2027. The central bank also maintained its commitment to take action against any spike in bond yields, such as increasing bond purchases flexibly.

The BOJ has explained that the June decision was not related to Ueda’s meeting with Takaichi.

However, a government official said, “The prime minister’s office appeared to view the decision as a trade-off under which the government accepted the rate hike in exchange for the BOJ revising its bond-buying plan.”

“If long-term bond yields climb further, the prime minister could seek larger bond purchases,” the official added.

Since ending its massive monetary easing program in March 2024, the BOJ has repeatedly said it would buy government bonds flexibly if yields surged. Still, it has not done so during any period of rising long-term yields.

If the BOJ resumes expanding its bond holdings in line with the government’s fiscal needs, financial markets could interpret the move as “fiscal financing,” in which a central bank effectively underwrites government deficits.

World.title: Japan to add five-year stay period for Type 2 foreign workers
World.content:
The Immigration Services Agency released a draft ministerial ordinance Tuesday to introduce a five-year period of stay for holders of the Type 2 specified skilled foreign worker status from early January next year after seeking public comments.

Holders of the status are currently granted periods of stay for six months, one year, two years or three years, depending on their employment stability, continuity and other factors. Longer periods carry stricter screening criteria, such as employment records and tax payment history.

The government said that detailed requirements for the new program will be finalized later.

The new five-year category would align with other residence statuses for foreign nationals, including those for nursing care workers, whose maximum stay period is five years.

Under the current guidelines for permanent residency status, applicants must hold the longest available period of stay under their current residence status.

World.title: Vietnamese man hints at murdering elderly woman in Saitama
World.content:
A Vietnamese national in his 30s has made a statement suggesting he killed a 91-year-old woman from Iruma, Saitama Prefecture, according to investigative sources.

Acting on the man’s statement, the Saitama Prefectural Police searched a forested area in Hanno, which neighbors Iruma, on Saturday night and found the body of Kinuko Maruyama, the sources said.

The man had been arrested after driving away from the woman’s home in a vehicle. The police suspect the possibility of murder and abandonment of a corpse.

Maruyama’s daughter reported to police on Friday that the 91-year-old, who lived alone, was missing.

When officers checked Maruyama’s house, the front door was unlocked and they found that a minivehicle registered to her son was missing. Maruyama did not have a driver’s license.

World.title: One week on, disaster response in Kumamoto shifts to helping survivors
World.content:
A week after a devastating earthquake registering shindo 7, the highest level on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, struck Kumamoto Prefecture, the disaster response is shifting from search and rescue to stabilizing survivors’ lives and preventing disaster-related casualties.

But uneven conditions across evacuation centers, where shortages of water and other essentials have been compounded by scorching summer heat, are raising fears of heatstroke and blood clots, medical experts said.

The latest prefectural tally shows the death toll from the July 28 earthquake remained at 38 as of Tuesday afternoon, while 123 had been injured. One is suspected to have died from heatstroke while taking refuge inside a car as temperatures in the region soared.

World.title: Europe’s wildfire season exposes climate insurance gap
World.content:
Domestic insurers are expected to absorb most of the losses from Europe’s worst wildfire season in recent history, but the blazes are also raising a bigger question: Who will pay as climate-driven disasters become more frequent and destructive?

Authorities have evacuated about 220,000 people in France as unprecedented wildfires burn across the country. Fires have also swept through Spain and Greece, fueling concerns about rising insurance costs and widening gaps in protection against climate-related risks. France’s total losses could ​reach €10 billion to €15 billion ($11.5 billion to $17.3 billion), with insured losses running into several billion euros, according to credit ratings agency Morningstar DBRS.

While manageable for ‌the ‌industry, analysts say the fires could offer a glimpse of the challenges ahead if blazes increasingly threaten densely populated areas.

World.title: Third-party probe finds Shogakukan ‘encouraged’ human rights violations
World.content:
A third-party panel at Shogakukan said Monday that the publisher encouraged human rights violations by hiring a male manga artist who had committed sexual misconduct as an author for a new series under a different pseudonym.

The panel said in an investigation report that Shogakukan’s manga app editorial department “encouraged and supported the violation of human rights of the female victim.”

The department changed the pen name of the male manga artist for the new series “Jojin Kamen” in 2022, according to the report. He had been fined for sexually assaulting a teenage girl who was his student when he was a teacher.

The report also said that the department changed the pseudonym of another male manga author when hiring him for new series “Seiso no Shinrishi,” even though his series in a different magazine was canceled after he was found guilty of sexual assault.

The panel pointed out that the “Jojin Kamen” author might not have been fully aware of the nature of the crime he committed. It criticized his editor for being involved in out-of-court settlement negotiations and deciding to publish the new series without sufficient investigation or review.

The report said that it is inevitable to conclude that the editor’s response “encouraged and supported the violation of human rights by the man against the victimized woman.”

Referring to the “Seiso no Shinrishi” case, the panel pointed out that the author had received psychological counseling. “It cannot be said that the decision to change the name was unreasonable” from the viewpoint of rehabilitation opportunities and privacy, the panel said.

It concluded that Shogakukan’s lack of sensitivity regarding preventing human rights violations was problematic. The company failed to “systematically assess, manage and supervise important risks.”

Shogakukan said in a statement that it sincerely apologizes to the victim, takes the matter very seriously and will face its responsibilities with sincerity.

World.title: Water dispenser linked to legionnaires’ disease case in private Hong Kong hospital
World.content:
An 89-year-old patient at the Hong Kong Sanatorium and Hospital is highly likely to have contracted legionnaires’ disease after drinking water from a contaminated dispenser, health authorities have said.

The Centre for Health Protection confirmed on Tuesday that samples from devices dispensing cooled boiled water at the private hospital in Happy Valley tested positive for Legionella pneumophila at levels far above the safety threshold for high‑risk areas of hospitals.

Genetic testing found that the bacteria matched the strain in the patient’s respiratory specimen.

The hospital has stopped using the affected dispensers. A total of 137 patients who stayed on the same floor as the infected man are under medical surveillance, but none has developed the disease.

Legionnaires’ disease is a severe, potentially life-threatening form of pneumonia caused by breathing in Legionella bacteria.

The patient had been hospitalised since April 1 for underlying illnesses, during which he occasionally experienced symptoms such as shortness of breath.

His shortness of breath worsened on July 6, prompting hospital staff to collect a respiratory specimen, which tested positive for Legionella pneumophila. The man’s condition improved following antibiotic treatment.

World.title: Lucky escape for boy, 7, after wheel comes off KMB double-decker bus in Hong Kong
World.content:
A seven-year-old boy escaped with minor injuries on Tuesday after a rear wheel came off a double-decker bus travelling on a busy road in Hong Kong’s Kowloon district.

Police received a report at 3.25pm that the KMB route 86 bus was travelling along Cheung Sha Wan Road towards Kwai Chung when its rear-left wheel became detached, just outside Cheung Sha Wan Plaza.

The wheel struck and dented a metal railing, which in turn hit the boy as he waited for a bus.

The boy was conscious and complained of soreness in his left thigh. He was taken to Caritas Medical Centre for treatment.

The 49-year-old driver surnamed Leung continued driving the bus for another 200 metres (656 feet) after the wheel came off before stopping. He passed the alcohol test.

A KMB spokesman told the South China Morning Post that Leung had inspected the vehicle before taking it out for duty and did not report any problems.

World.title: Beauty queen Grace Chan files police report after son splashed at cinema over row
World.content:
Hong Kong police are searching for a woman who allegedly splashed a “cream-like” liquid on the six‑year‑old son of actress and beauty queen Grace Chan Hoi‑lam at a cinema in Admiralty, following a dispute over the child’s behaviour during a movie screening.

A police source said on Tuesday that Chan, winner of the Miss Hong Kong 2013 pageant and wife of TVB actor Kevin Cheng Ka‑wing, filed a report with the force last Friday for splashing an “unknown liquid” on her son.

She was watching the summer blockbuster Spider‑Man: Brand New Day with her three sons, aged three, six and seven, at Pacific Place last Thursday afternoon.

On social media, an audience member said the children kept talking loudly, laughed and screamed throughout the film, prompting the user to repeatedly shush the boys even as their mother completely ignored them.

“Only when the lights came on at the end of the movie did I realise the mother was Grace Chan. As a celebrity, you don’t even know basic cinema etiquette and show zero respect for movies,” the viewer said.

The six‑year‑old was also said to have kicked the seat in front.

World.title: Boy, 7, dies in Hong Kong’s first fatal paediatric flu case of 2026
World.content:
Hong Kong recorded the first fatal paediatric case of influenza this year after a seven-year-old boy died on Tuesday, nine days after displaying symptoms.

The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) said that the boy, who had been in good health, developed a cough and runny nose on July 27 and a fever on Saturday, before his condition deteriorated on Monday when he became less responsive.

He was admitted in critical condition to the paediatric intensive care unit at Princess Margaret Hospital in Kwai Chung on Monday, where a respiratory specimen tested positive for influenza A (H3) virus.

The boy was diagnosed with influenza A infection complicated by shock and encephalopathy, a group of conditions that can cause brain dysfunction. He died on Tuesday.

The child had received a seasonal influenza vaccination under the 2025-26 scheme.

While the boy had not travelled during the incubation period, a household contact had earlier tested positive for influenza and recovered after a mild illness.

World.title: Hong Kong, Macau police arrest 8 over HK$100m Vietnam coffee investment scam
World.content:
Hong Kong and Macau police have arrested eight people in a crackdown on an investment scam syndicate that cheated more than 200 people out of nearly HK$100 million (US$12.75 million) by promoting itself as a pioneer of “kinetic coffee philosophy”.

The syndicate, operating under the name Fun Coffee, established a presence in Hong Kong last year.

Fun Coffee says on its website that it is a coffee investment enterprise based in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, with assets of more than US$1 billion and a team of more than 5,000.

On the English-language website, which remained live on Tuesday, Fun Coffee describes itself as a pioneer of “kinetic coffee philosophy” and promotes what it called the world’s first “sports-coffee-value ecosystem”, offering customised coffee-based nutritional support to runners.

As of Monday, Hong Kong police said they had received 225 complaints from potential victims since last month, involving investments ranging from HK$3,000 to HK$9.63 million, totalling HK$94 million.

The victims, aged 32 to 83 and including retirees, said they were invited to download the Fun Coffee app before investing in virtual currency.

World.title: Over 1,000 sign up for Hong Kong’s new taxi, ride-hailing test
World.content:
More than 1,000 applicants have registered for a new combined test for taxi and ride-hailing services in Hong Kong, with lawmakers expecting more people to sign up to meet demand for drivers once the city’s ride-hailing regulatory regime takes effect next year.

The initial response came after the Transport Department replaced the stand-alone taxi driver exam with the new combined test, which allows successful candidates to apply for a taxi driving licence or a ride-hailing vehicle permit after attending relevant courses.

The department said the response had been “positive”, with more than 1,000 online applications as of 6pm on Monday, the first day of registration. It said it would organise additional examination sessions depending on demand.

Ben Chan Han-pan, chairman of the Legislative Council’s transport panel, said on Tuesday that he believed more people would 

“This test will allow them to drive taxi and ride-hailing vehicles legally ... I believe the number of candidates will gradually increase,” he said.

Mark Chong Ho-fung, a member of Legco’s transport panel, said the combined written test had been well received as expected, adding that the industry had also seen more applications for the former taxi written test as drivers prepared in advance.

World.title: Security at reservoir ramped up after trespassers enter spillway during discharge
World.content:
Hong Kong authorities have set up fences and surveillance cameras at a reservoir and warned they could take legal action against trespassers, after a group was filmed entering a spillway to take photos while the facility was discharging water.

A South China Morning Post reporter observed on Tuesday that two barriers and a surveillance camera had been set up at Ho Pui Reservoir in Tai Lam.

After footage of the trespassers went viral over the weekend, the Water Supplies Department said it was highly concerned about the alleged incident and warned it would prosecute offenders if there was sufficient evidence.

“The department will seriously follow up on the video showing rule violations that is circulated on social media, and launch an investigation. If there is sufficient evidence, we will consult the Department of Justice and press charges,” a spokesman said.

CCTV installed at Hong Kong reservoir after viral video of hikers posing for photos

He added that the department had erected warning signs in the catchment area and other locations near the reservoir to remind hikers and other visitors not to enter the facility, and would boost law enforcement operations at the site.

World.title: Jardines ending Oxbridge undergrad scholarships to ‘maximise impact’ for more students
World.content:
Hong Kong-based conglomerate Jardine Matheson has said it ended a 44-year-old undergraduate scholarship programme for Oxford and Cambridge universities to “maximise impact” for more students, while a former recipient has called the scheme a “life-changing” opportunity.

Students starting their studies later this year will be the final cohort of “Oxbridge” undergraduates covered by the programme, according to the website of the Jardine Foundation, the company’s education trust.

In a reply to the South China Morning Post on Tuesday, Jardine Matheson said it was increasing its “focus and commitment” on the Asian market and that the decision was made to support the region.

“This change is purely driven by being able to maximise impact for the greatest number of students,” it said.

“As with all organisations, Jardine Foundation regularly reviews its approach to assess whether its programmes and initiatives are fulfilling its objectives as effectively as possible.”

The company added that the foundation was focused on making the best possible impact in the communities where its businesses operated.

The move marks the end of an undergraduate scholarship programme that has operated for 44 years.

World.title: Education, health fees among key concerns
World.content:
China to legislate on preschool education

China will push for legislation on preschool education to provide a legal guarantee for the operation and management of such institutions, Vice-minister of Education Tian Xuejun said on Nov 30.

Tian made the remarks at a news conference organized by the State Council Information Office regarding a child abuse case at RYB Education New World Kindergarten in Beijing that received widespread attention in November. He said the Ministry of Education was already doing research on the legislation.

"The ministry will also complete the requirements on qualifications of teachers engaged in preschool education and is considering formulating a code of ethics for them," Tian said.

He also said a plan is on the way to step up supervision of kindergartens and solve the problem of insufficient resources for preschool education. Tian said the case exposed the conflict between public demand for preschool enrollment and insufficient development of preschool education.

"It also showed that some local authorities and kindergartens still have problems of unsound management and failure to implement or fully implement regulations," he said.

Rural health fee increase explained in detail
